bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第200卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 200
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 200

sentences.zh: 【唐紀十六】起旃蒙單瘀十月，盡玄勣閹茂七月，凡六年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 16] Beginning in the tenth month of the year zhānméng-dānyū, ending in the seventh month of the year xuánjì-yǎnmào — altogether a little over six years.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 16] Spanning from the tenth month of 656 through the seventh month of 662 — a period of just over six years.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己酉，下詔稱：「王皇后、蕭淑妃謀行鴆毒，廢為庶人，母及兄弟，並除名，流嶺南。」

translations.literal: “In winter, the tenth month, on the day jǐyǒu, an edict was issued stating: 'Empress Wang and Consort Xiao plotted to administer poison; they are deposed to commoner status, and their mother and brothers are all struck from the registers and exiled to Lingnan.'”
translations.idiomatic: “In winter, the tenth month, on the day jǐyǒu, an edict declared that Empress Wang and Consort Xiao had plotted poisoning and were degraded to commoners, while their mother and brothers were struck from the family register and banished to Lingnan.”

sentences.zh: 許敬宗奏：「故特進贈司空王仁祐告身尚存，使逆亂餘孽猶得為廕，並請除削。」

translations.literal: “Xu Jingzong memorialized: 'The commission document of the late specially advanced and posthumously appointed Minister of Works Wang Renyou still survives, allowing the remnants of the rebellious faction to claim hereditary privilege; I request that these be revoked as well.'”
translations.idiomatic: “Xu Jingzong memorialized that Wang Renyou's commission papers still survived, enabling the remnants of the disgraced faction to claim hereditary privileges, and asked that these honors be revoked as well.”

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，百官上表請立中宮，乃下詔曰：「武氏門著勳庸，地華纓黻，往以才行選入後庭，譽重椒闈，德光蘭掖。

translations.literal: “On the day yǐmǎo, the officials submitted a memorial requesting the installation of an empress; an edict was then issued stating: 'The Wu clan is distinguished in merit and service, noble in rank and station. Formerly selected into the inner palace for talent and conduct, her reputation was weighty in the women's quarters and her virtue shone in the orchid chambers.
translations.idiomatic: “On the day yǐmǎo, the officials petitioned for the installation of an empress, and an edict was issued praising the Wu clan's distinguished service and noble standing, noting that she had been selected into the inner palace for her talent and conduct and had won renown in the women's quarters.

sentences.zh: 朕昔在儲貳，特荷先慈，常得待從，弗離朝夕，宮壺之內，恆自飭躬，嬪嬙之間，未嘗迕目，聖情鑒悉，每垂賞歎，遂以武氏賜朕，事同政君，可立為皇后。」

translations.literal: When I was crown prince, I was especially favored by my late mother, who always had Lady Wu attend me and never leave my side day or night. Within the inner palace she constantly restrained herself; among the consorts she never met my gaze improperly. The late empress perceived this and often praised her. Lady Wu was therefore bestowed upon me, in the manner of Lady Zheng, and may be installed as empress.'"
translations.idiomatic: When I was crown prince, my late mother favored Lady Wu, who attended me constantly day and night. Within the palace she conducted herself with restraint, and among the consorts she never met my gaze improperly. The late empress noticed this and often praised her. Lady Wu was therefore given to me, as Lady Zheng had been to a former emperor, and may now be installed as empress."
translations.footnote: Closing quotation mark in the source

sentences.zh: 丁巳，赦天下。

translations.literal: On the day dīngsì, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dīngsì, the emperor proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 是日，皇后上表稱：「陛下前以妾為宸妃，韓瑗、來濟面折庭爭，此既事之極難，豈非深情為國！

translations.literal: “That same day, the empress submitted a memorial stating: 'Your Majesty previously wished to make your servant a Lady of the Bright Hall; Han Yuan and Lai Ji argued against it face to face in court. This was already the utmost difficulty of the matter — was it not deep devotion to the state!
translations.idiomatic: “That same day, the new empress submitted a memorial saying that when the emperor had wished to make her a Lady of the Bright Hall, Han Yuan and Lai Ji had argued against it in open court — a matter of the utmost difficulty that surely reflected their deep devotion to the state.

sentences.zh: 乞加褒賞。」

translations.literal: I beg that they be granted rewards and commendation.'"
translations.idiomatic: She asked that they be rewarded and commended."

sentences.zh: 上以表示瑗等，瑗等彌憂懼，屢請去位，上不許。

translations.literal: The emperor showed the memorial to Yuan and the others; they became all the more anxious and fearful, repeatedly requesting to resign their posts, but the emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed the memorial to Han Yuan and his colleagues, who grew still more anxious and fearful and repeatedly asked to resign, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁卯朔，臨軒命司空李勣繼璽綬冊皇后武氏。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, dīngmǎo, the emperor took his seat at the imperial hall and ordered Minister of Works Li Jì to receive the imperial seal and sash and invest Lady Wu as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the first day dīngmǎo, the emperor presided at the imperial hall and ordered Li Jì, Minister of Works, to invest Lady Wu as empress with the imperial seal and sash.

sentences.zh: 是日，百官朝皇后於肅義門。

translations.literal: That same day, the officials paid court to the empress at the Suyi Gate.
translations.idiomatic: That same day, the officials paid their respects to the empress at the Suyi Gate.

sentences.zh: 故后王氏、故淑妃蕭氏，並囚於別院，上嘗念之，間行至其所，見其室封閉極密，惟竅壁以通食器，惻然傷之，呼曰：「皇后、淑妃安在？」

translations.literal: The former empress Wang and the former Consort Xiao were both imprisoned in a separate courtyard. The emperor sometimes thought of them and went privately to their place. Seeing their rooms sealed extremely tight, with only holes in the walls to pass food vessels, he was moved with pity and called out: 'Where are the empress and the consort?'
translations.idiomatic: The deposed Empress Wang and Consort Xiao were held in a separate courtyard. The emperor sometimes thought of them and went to see them in secret. Finding their rooms sealed tight, with food passed only through holes in the walls, he was moved with pity and called out, 'Where are the empress and the consort?'

sentences.zh: 王氏泣對曰：「妾等得罪為宮婢，何得更有尊稱！」

translations.literal: Wang wept and replied: 'We have offended and are palace maids — how can we still bear honored titles!'
translations.idiomatic: Wang wept and replied, 'We have offended and are mere palace maids — how can we still bear such honored titles!'

sentences.zh: 又曰：「至尊若念疇昔，使妾等再見日月，乞名此院為回心院。」

translations.literal: She added: 'If Your Majesty remembers the past and allows us to see the sun and moon again, I beg that this courtyard be named the Courtyard of Returning Hearts.'
translations.idiomatic: She added, 'If Your Majesty remembers the past and allows us to see daylight again, I beg that this courtyard be named the Courtyard of Returning Hearts.'

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕即有處置。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'I shall presently make arrangements.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'I shall see to it presently.'

sentences.zh: 武后聞之，大怒，遣人杖王氏及蕭氏各一百，斷去手足，捉酒甕中，曰：「令二嫗骨醉！」

translations.literal: When Empress Wu heard of this, she was furious and sent men to beat Wang and Xiao each a hundred strokes, cut off their hands and feet, and place them in wine jars, saying: 'Let the two old hags' bones be steeped in wine!'
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu heard of this, she was furious and sent men to beat Wang and Xiao a hundred strokes each, cut off their hands and feet, and place them in wine jars, saying, 'Let the two old hags steep their bones in wine!'

sentences.zh: 數日而死，又斬之。

translations.literal: After several days they died, and their bodies were then beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: They died within several days, and their bodies were then beheaded.

sentences.zh: 王氏初聞宣敕，再拜曰：「願大家萬歲！

translations.literal: When Wang first heard the imperial decree announced, she bowed twice and said: 'May Her Majesty live ten thousand years!
translations.idiomatic: When Wang first heard the decree announced, she bowed twice and said, 'May Her Majesty live ten thousand years!

sentences.zh: 昭儀承恩，死自吾分。」

translations.literal: The Lady of Bright Deportment enjoys the emperor's favor; death is my own portion.'
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Bright Deportment enjoys the emperor's favor; death is my own due.'

sentences.zh: 淑妃罵曰：「阿武妖猾，乃至於此！

translations.literal: Consort Xiao cursed: 'That witch Wu is so treacherous as to come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Consort Xiao cursed, 'That witch Wu is so treacherous as to come to this!

sentences.zh: 願他生我為貓，阿武為鼠，生生扼其喉。」

translations.literal: May I be reborn as a cat and Wu as a mouse, and in life after life throttle her throat.'
translations.idiomatic: May I be reborn as a cat and Wu as a mouse, and in life after life throttle her throat.'

sentences.zh: 由是宮中不畜貓。

translations.literal: From this time cats were not kept in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: From that time onward, cats were not kept in the palace.

sentences.zh: 尋又改王氏姓為蟒氏，蕭氏為梟氏。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Wang's clan name was changed to Mǎng ('python') and Xiao's to Xiāo ('owl').
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Wang's clan name was changed to Python and Xiao's to Owl.

sentences.zh: 武后數見王、蕭為祟，被髮瀝血如死時狀。

translations.literal: Empress Wu repeatedly saw Wang and Xiao as malevolent spirits, hair disheveled and dripping blood as at the time of their deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu repeatedly saw Wang and Xiao as vengeful spirits, hair disheveled and dripping blood as they had been at death.

sentences.zh: 後徙居蓬萊宮，復見之，故多在洛陽，終身不歸長安。

translations.literal: Later, when she moved to Penglai Palace, she saw them again; therefore she mostly stayed in Luoyang and never returned to Chang'an for the rest of her life.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when she moved to Penglai Palace, she saw them again; thereafter she spent most of her time in Luoyang and never returned to Chang'an for the rest of her life.

sentences.zh: 己巳，許敬宗奏曰：「永徽爰始，國本未生，權引彗星，越升明兩。

translations.literal: “On the day jǐsì, Xu Jingzong memorialized: 'Since the Yonghui era began, the foundation of the state had not yet been secured; a comet was provisionally invoked to ascend beyond the bright pair.
translations.idiomatic: “On the day jǐsì, Xu Jingzong memorialized that since the Yonghui era the succession had not been settled, and a comet — a provisional heir — had been elevated beyond the proper line.

sentences.zh: 近者元妃載誕，正胤降神，重光日融，爝暉宜息。

translations.literal: Recently the primary consort has given birth, and the legitimate heir has descended from heaven; the doubled radiance of the sun grows warm, and the torchlight should be extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the primary consort has given birth to the legitimate heir, and the sun's doubled radiance grows warm — the torchlight of a provisional heir should now be extinguished.

sentences.zh: 安可反植枝幹，久易位於天庭；

translations.literal: How can one plant the branches upside down and long exchange positions in the heavenly court;
translations.idiomatic: How can the branches be planted upside down and positions long exchanged in the heavenly court;

sentences.zh: 倒襲裳衣，使違方於震位！

translations.literal: invert the lower and upper garments, making them violate their proper places in the eastern quadrant!
translations.idiomatic: or the garments be worn upside down, violating their proper stations in the eastern quadrant!

sentences.zh: 又，父子之際，人所難言，事或犯鱗，必嬰嚴憲，煎膏染鼎，臣亦甘心。」

translations.literal: Furthermore, between father and son is a matter men find hard to speak of; if the affair should touch the dragon's scales, I must incur severe punishment — to be boiled in oil or dyed in the cauldron, your servant would accept it willingly.'"
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, the relationship between father and son is difficult to address; if I should touch a forbidden matter and incur severe punishment — even boiling in oil — I would accept it willingly."

sentences.zh: 上召見，問之，對曰：「皇太子，國之本也，本猶未正，萬國無所繫心。

translations.literal: “The emperor summoned him for an audience and questioned him. He replied: 'The crown prince is the foundation of the state; when the foundation is not yet set right, the myriad states have nothing to anchor their hearts to.
translations.idiomatic: “The emperor summoned him and questioned him. He replied that the crown prince was the foundation of the state, and until that foundation was set right, the realm had nothing to anchor its loyalty to.

sentences.zh: 且在東宮者，所出本微，今知國家已有正嫡，必不自安。

translations.literal: Moreover, the one now in the Eastern Palace is of humble birth; now that he knows the state already has a legitimate heir, he will surely not feel secure in his position.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the prince now in the Eastern Palace is of humble birth; now that he knows the state has a legitimate heir, he will surely not feel secure.

sentences.zh: 竊位而懷自疑，恐非宗廟之福，願陛下熟計之。」

translations.literal: To usurp a position while harboring self-doubt — I fear this is not a blessing for the ancestral temple; I beg Your Majesty to consider this carefully.'"
translations.idiomatic: To hold a position while filled with self-doubt cannot be a blessing for the ancestral temple; I beg Your Majesty to consider this carefully."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「忠已自讓。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Zhong has already yielded of his own accord.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'Zhong has already yielded of his own accord.'

sentences.zh: 對曰：「能為太伯，願速從之。」

translations.literal: He replied: 'If he can be like Taibo, I hope he will do so swiftly.'
translations.idiomatic: He replied, 'If he can be like Taibo, I hope he will do so at once.'
translations.footnote: Closing quotation mark in the source

sentences.zh: 西突厥頡苾達度設數遣使請兵討沙缽羅可汗。

translations.literal: The Western Türk chieftain Ashina Dadu she repeatedly sent envoys requesting troops to attack the qaghan Shabo.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Türk chieftain Ashina Dadu she repeatedly sent envoys requesting troops to attack Qaghan Shabo.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，遣豐州都督元禮臣冊拜頡苾達度設為可汗。

translations.literal: On the day jiǎxū, Yuan Lichen, military governor of Feng Prefecture, was dispatched to invest Ashina Dadu she as qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiǎxū, Yuan Lichen, military governor of Feng Prefecture, was dispatched to invest Ashina Dadu she as qaghan.

sentences.zh: 禮臣至碎葉城，沙缽羅發兵拒之，不得前。

translations.literal: When Lichen reached Suyab, Shabo raised troops to resist him, and he could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Lichen reached Suyab, Shabo raised troops to block him, and he could not advance.

sentences.zh: 頡苾達度設部落多為沙缽羅所並，餘眾寡弱，不為諸姓所附，禮臣竟不冊拜而歸。

translations.literal: Most of Ashina Dadu she's tribes had been absorbed by Shabo; the remaining followers were few and weak and not attached to by the various clans, so Lichen ultimately returned without performing the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Most of Ashina Dadu she's tribes had been absorbed by Shabo; the survivors were few and weak and won no support from the other clans, so Lichen returned without performing the investiture.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎李義府參知政事。

translations.literal: Li Yifu, Vice Director of the Secretariat, was appointed to participate in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yifu, Vice Director of the Secretariat, was appointed to participate in governing.

sentences.zh: 義府容貌溫恭，與人語，必嬉怡微笑，而狡險忌克，故時人謂義府笑中有刀；

translations.literal: Yifu had a gentle and respectful appearance; whenever he spoke with others he would smile cheerfully, yet he was treacherous, dangerous, jealous, and spiteful, so people of the time said Yifu had a knife in his smile;
translations.idiomatic: Yifu had a gentle, respectful appearance and always smiled cheerfully when speaking with others, yet he was treacherous, jealous, and spiteful, so people said he had a knife in his smile;

sentences.zh: 又以其柔而害物，謂之李貓。

translations.literal: and because his softness harmed others, they called him Li the Cat.
translations.idiomatic: and because his soft manner harmed others, they called him Li the Cat.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛未，以皇太子忠為梁王、梁州刺史，立皇后子代王弘為皇太子，生四年矣。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day xīngwèi, Crown Prince Zhong was made Prince of Liang and military governor of Liang Prefecture; the empress's son, Prince Dai Hong, was installed as crown prince — he was four years old.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the day xīngwèi, Crown Prince Zhong was made Prince of Liang and military governor of Liang Prefecture, while the empress's son, Prince Dai Hong, was installed as crown prince at the age of four.

sentences.zh: 忠既廢，官屬皆懼罪亡匿，無敢見者；

translations.literal: Once Zhong was deposed, his staff all feared punishment and fled into hiding; none dared to see him;
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhong was deposed, his staff all feared punishment and fled; none dared to see him;

sentences.zh: 右庶子李安仁獨候忠，泣涕拜辭而去。

translations.literal: only the Right Guardian of the Heir Apparent Li Anren alone waited for Zhong, weeping and bowing in farewell before departing.
translations.idiomatic: only Li Anren, Right Guardian of the Heir Apparent, waited for him, weeping and bowing in farewell before departing.

sentences.zh: 安仁，綱之孫也。

translations.literal: Anren was a grandson of Li Gang.
translations.idiomatic: Anren was a grandson of Li Gang.

sentences.zh: 壬申，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: On the day rénshēn, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the reign era was changed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day rénshēn, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the reign era was changed.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛亥，贈武士擭司徒，賜爵周國公。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day xīnghài, Wu Shiyue was posthumously appointed Minister of Works and granted the title Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day xīnghài, Wu Shiyue was posthumously appointed Minister of Works and granted the title Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，以度支侍郎杜正倫為黃門侍郎、同三品。

translations.literal: In the third month, Du Zhenglun, Vice Director of the Revenue Bureau, was appointed Vice Director of the Chancellery with the rank of Tong Sanpin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Du Zhenglun, Vice Director of the Revenue Bureau, was appointed Vice Director of the Chancellery with third-rank status.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬子，矩州人謝無靈舉兵反，黔州都督李子和討平之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day rénzǐ, Xie Wuling of Ju Prefecture raised troops in rebellion; Li Zihe, military governor of Qian Prefecture, suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the day rénzǐ, Xie Wuling of Ju Prefecture rebelled; Li Zihe, military governor of Qian Prefecture, suppressed the uprising.

sentences.zh: 己未，上謂侍臣曰：「朕思養人之道，未得其要，公等為朕陳之。」

translations.literal: On the day jǐwèi, the emperor said to his attending ministers: 'I have been considering the way to nurture the people but have not grasped its essentials; explain them to me.'
translations.idiomatic: On the day jǐwèi, the emperor told his ministers, 'I have been considering how best to nurture the people but have not grasped the essentials; explain them to me.'

sentences.zh: 來濟對曰：「昔齊桓公出遊，見老而饑寒者，命賜之食，老人曰：『願賜一國之饑者。』

translations.literal: Lai Ji replied: 'Formerly Duke Huan of Qi went out on a tour and saw an old man suffering from hunger and cold. He ordered food given to him. The old man said: "I wish you would give food to all the hungry in the state.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Ji replied with a story: Duke Huan of Qi once saw an old man suffering from hunger and cold and ordered food given to him. The old man said, 'I wish you would feed all the hungry in the state.

sentences.zh: 賜之衣，曰：『願賜一國之寒者。』

translations.literal: He gave him clothing, and the man said: 'I wish you would clothe all the cold in the state.'
translations.idiomatic: He gave him clothing, and the man said, 'I wish you would clothe all the cold in the state.'

sentences.zh: 公曰：『寡人之廩府安足以週一國之饑寒！』

translations.literal: The duke said: 'How can my granaries possibly suffice for all the hunger and cold in the state!'
translations.idiomatic: The duke said, 'How can my granaries possibly suffice for all the hunger and cold in the state!'

sentences.zh: 老人曰『君不奪農時，則國人皆有餘食矣；

translations.literal: The old man said: 'If the ruler does not seize the farming seasons, then the people of the state will all have surplus food;
translations.idiomatic: The old man said, 'If the ruler does not seize the farming seasons, the people will all have surplus food;

sentences.zh: 不奪蠶要，則國人皆有餘衣矣！』

translations.literal: if he does not seize the silkworm seasons, then the people of the state will all have surplus clothing!'
translations.idiomatic: if he does not seize the silkworm seasons, the people will all have surplus clothing!'

sentences.zh: 故人君之養人，在省其征役而已。

translations.literal: Therefore the ruler's way of nurturing the people lies simply in reducing their corvée labor and levies.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the ruler's way of nurturing the people lies simply in reducing their corvée labor and levies.

sentences.zh: 今山東役丁，歲別數萬，役之則人大勞，取庸則人大費。

translations.literal: Now in the east, corvée laborers number tens of thousands each year; if they are conscripted, the people are greatly exhausted, and if substitute payments are taken, the people are greatly impoverished.
translations.idiomatic: Today in the east, corvée laborers number tens of thousands each year; conscription exhausts the people, and substitute payments impoverish them.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下量公家所須外，餘悉免之。」

translations.literal: Your servant wishes that Your Majesty, beyond what the state genuinely requires, would exempt all the rest.'
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty, beyond what the state genuinely requires, to exempt all the rest.'

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 六月，辛亥，禮宮奏停太祖、世祖配祀，以高祖配昊天於圜丘，太宗配五帝於明堂；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day xīnghài, the ritual officials memorialized to discontinue the joint sacrifices to the High Ancestor and the Founding Ancestor, assigning Emperor Gaozu to accompany the Supreme Lord of Heaven at the Circular Mound and Emperor Taizong to accompany the Five Emperors at the Bright Hall;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day xīnghài, the ritual officials memorialized to discontinue joint sacrifices to the High Ancestor and Founding Ancestor, assigning Emperor Gaozu to accompany the Supreme Lord of Heaven at the Circular Mound and Emperor Taizong to accompany the Five Emperors at the Bright Hall;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，乙丑，西洱蠻酋長楊棟附、顯和蠻酋長王羅祁、郎、昆、梨、盤四州酋長王伽沖等帥眾內附。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day yǐchǒu, Yang Dongfu, chieftain of the Western Erhai tribes, Wang Luoqi, chieftain of the Xianhe tribes, and Wang Jiachong, chieftain of the four prefectures of Lang, Kun, Li, and Pan, among others, led their followers in submitting to Tang rule.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day yǐchǒu, chieftains Yang Dongfu of the Western Erhai tribes, Wang Luoqi of the Xianhe tribes, and Wang Jiachong of the four prefectures of Lang, Kun, Li, and Pan, among others, led their followers in submitting to Tang rule.

sentences.zh: 癸未，以中書令崔敦禮為太子少師、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: On the day guǐwèi, Cui Dunli, Director of the Secretariat, was appointed Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince with the rank of Tong Zhongshu Menxia Sanpin.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guǐwèi, Cui Dunli, Director of the Secretariat, was appointed Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince with third-rank chancellery status.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙申，固安昭公崔敦禮薨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day bǐngshēn, Cui Dunli, Duke of Gu'an with the posthumous title Zhao, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day bǐngshēn, Cui Dunli, Duke of Gu'an, died.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，蔥山道行軍總管程知節擊西突厥，與歌邏、處月二部戰於榆慕谷，大破之，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: On the day xīnchǒu, Cheng Zhijie, commander of the Onion Mountain campaign, attacked the Western Türks and fought the Geluolu and Chuyue tribes at Yumugu Valley, routing them utterly and taking more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xīnchǒu, Cheng Zhijie, commander of the Onion Mountain campaign, attacked the Western Türks and defeated the Geluolu and Chuyue tribes at Yumugu Valley, taking more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 副總管周智度攻突騎施、處木昆等部於咽城，拔之，斬首三萬級。

translations.literal: Deputy commander Zhou Zhidu attacked the Turgesh, Chumukun, and other tribes at Yancheng, captured it, and took thirty thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander Zhou Zhidu attacked the Turgesh, Chumukun, and other tribes at Yancheng, captured the city, and took thirty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，龜茲王布失畢入朝。

translations.literal: On the day yǐsì, the king of Kucha, Bushibi, came to court.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yǐsì, Bushibi, king of Kucha, came to court.

sentences.zh: 李義府恃寵用事。

translations.literal: Li Yifu relied on imperial favor to wield power.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yifu relied on imperial favor to wield power.

sentences.zh: 洛州婦人淳于氏，美色，系大理獄，義府屬大理寺丞畢正義枉法出之，將納為妾，大理卿段寶玄疑而奏之。

translations.literal: A woman of Luoyang surnamed Chunyu, of striking beauty, was held in the Court of Judicial Review prison. Yifu instructed Vice Director Bi Zhengyi of the Court of Judicial Review to release her unlawfully, intending to take her as a concubine. Director Duan Baoxuan grew suspicious and memorialized the matter.
translations.idiomatic: A beautiful woman of Luoyang surnamed Chunyu was held in the Court of Judicial Review prison. Yifu had Vice Director Bi Zhengyi release her unlawfully, intending to take her as a concubine. Director Duan Baoxuan grew suspicious and reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 上命給事中劉仁軌等鞫之，義府恐事洩，逼正義自縊於獄中。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Attendant Liu Rengui and others to investigate. Yifu, fearing the affair would be exposed, forced Zhengyi to hang himself in prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Liu Rengui and others to investigate. Yifu, fearing exposure, forced Zhengyi to hang himself in prison.

sentences.zh: 上知之，原義府罪不問。

translations.literal: The emperor learned of this but pardoned Yifu and did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor learned of this but pardoned Yifu and took no action.

sentences.zh: 侍御史漣水王義方欲奏彈之，先白其母曰：「義方為御史，視奸臣不糾則不忠，糾之則身危而憂及於親為不孝，二者不能自決，奈何？」

translations.literal: Attending Censor Wang Yifang of Lianshui wished to impeach him and first told his mother: 'As a censor, if I see a treacherous minister and do not impeach him I am disloyal; if I impeach him my person is endangered and my kin are imperiled, which is unfilial. I cannot decide between the two — what am I to do?'
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Wang Yifang of Lianshui wished to impeach him and first told his mother, 'As a censor, if I see a treacherous minister and do not impeach him I am disloyal; if I impeach him I endanger myself and my family, which is unfilial. I cannot decide between the two — what am I to do?'

sentences.zh: 母曰：「昔王陵之母，殺身以成子之名。

translations.literal: His mother said: 'Formerly the mother of Wang Ling gave her life to establish her son's reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His mother said, 'Formerly the mother of Wang Ling gave her life to establish her son's reputation.

sentences.zh: 汝能盡忠以事君，吾死不恨！」

translations.literal: If you can serve the ruler with full loyalty, I shall die without regret!'
translations.idiomatic: If you can serve the ruler with full loyalty, I shall die without regret!'

sentences.zh: 義方乃奏稱：「義府於輦轂之下，擅殺六品寺丞；

translations.literal: “Yifang then memorialized: 'Yifu, beneath the imperial capital, arbitrarily killed a sixth-rank vice director of the court;
translations.idiomatic: “Yifang then memorialized that Yifu, beneath the imperial capital, had arbitrarily killed a sixth-rank vice director;

sentences.zh: 就雲正義自殺，亦由畏義府威，殺身以滅口。

translations.literal: even if one says Zhengyi killed himself, it was also from fear of Yifu's power — he gave his life to silence the affair.
translations.idiomatic: even if Zhengyi killed himself, it was from fear of Yifu's power — he gave his life to silence the affair.

sentences.zh: 如此，則生殺之威，不由上出，漸不可長，請更加勘當！」

translations.literal: In this way the power of life and death no longer issues from the throne; such a trend cannot be allowed to grow — I beg that the matter be investigated further!'
translations.idiomatic: In this way the power of life and death no longer issues from the throne; such a trend cannot be allowed to grow — I beg that the matter be investigated further!'

sentences.zh: 於是對仗，叱義府令下；

translations.literal: Thereupon, facing the imperial audience, the emperor shouted at Yifu to step down;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon, facing the imperial audience, the emperor shouted at Yifu to step down;

sentences.zh: 義府顧望不退。

translations.literal: Yifu looked about and would not withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu looked about and would not withdraw.

sentences.zh: 義方三叱，上既無言，義府始趨出，義方乃讀彈文。

translations.literal: Yifang shouted three times; when the emperor remained silent, Yifu at last hurried out, and Yifang then read his impeachment memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Yifang shouted three times; when the emperor remained silent, Yifu at last hurried out, and Yifang then read his impeachment memorial.

sentences.zh: 上釋義府不問，而謂義方毀辱大臣，言辭不遜，貶萊州司戶。

translations.literal: The emperor released Yifu without inquiry but said Yifang had insulted a high minister with impertinent language and demoted him to Registrar of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor released Yifu without inquiry but demoted Yifang to Registrar of Laizhou for insulting a high minister with impertinent language.

sentences.zh: 九月，括州暴風，海溢，溺四千餘家。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, a violent storm struck Kuo Prefecture; the sea overflowed and drowned more than four thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, a violent storm struck Kuo Prefecture; the sea overflowed and drowned more than four thousand households.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，丙寅，生羌酋長浪我利波等帥眾內附，以其地置柘、栱二州。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on the day bǐngyín, Lang Wolibo and other chieftains of the Sheng Qiang led their followers in submitting to Tang rule; their territory was organized as the two prefectures of Zhe and Gong.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on the day bǐngyín, Lang Wolibo and other chieftains of the Sheng Qiang led their followers in submitting to Tang rule, and their territory was organized as the prefectures of Zhe and Gong.

sentences.zh: 十二月，程知節引軍至鷹娑川，遇西突厥二萬騎，別部鼠尼施等二萬餘騎繼至，前軍總管蘇定方帥五百騎馳往擊之，西突厥大敗，追奔二十里，殺獲千五百餘人，獲馬及器械，綿亙山野，不可勝計。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Cheng Zhijie led his army to the Yingsuo River and encountered twenty thousand Western Türk cavalry; another twenty thousand or more cavalry of the Shunishi and other divisions arrived in succession. Vanguard commander Su Dingfang led five hundred horsemen in a charge against them; the Western Türks were utterly defeated. Pursuing them twenty li, they killed and captured more than fifteen hundred men and seized horses and weapons stretching across the mountains and plains beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Cheng Zhijie led his army to the Yingsuo River and encountered twenty thousand Western Türk cavalry, with another twenty thousand or more of the Shunishi division arriving in succession. Vanguard commander Su Dingfang led five hundred horsemen in a charge; the Western Türks were utterly defeated. Pursuing them twenty li, they killed and captured more than fifteen hundred men and seized horses and weapons stretching across the mountains and plains beyond count.

sentences.zh: 副大總管王文度害其功，言於知節曰：「今茲雖雲破賊，官軍亦有死傷，乘危輕脫，乃成敗之法耳，何急而為此！

translations.literal: Deputy supreme commander Wang Wendu, envious of his achievement, said to Zhijie: 'Though we have broken the enemy this time, our own troops also suffered casualties. To press an advantage recklessly is the way of victory and defeat — why be so hasty!
translations.idiomatic: Deputy supreme commander Wang Wendu, envious of his achievement, said to Zhijie, 'Though we broke the enemy this time, our own troops also suffered casualties. To press an advantage recklessly courts disaster — why be so hasty!

sentences.zh: 自今當結方陳，置輜重在內，遇賊則戰，此萬全策也。」

translations.literal: From now on we should form square formations, place the baggage train within, and fight only when we encounter the enemy — this is the strategy of complete security.'
translations.idiomatic: From now on we should form square formations, keep the baggage train within, and fight only when we encounter the enemy — that is the surest strategy.'

sentences.zh: 又矯稱別得旨，以知節恃勇輕敵，委文度為之節制，遂收軍不許深入。

translations.literal: He also falsely claimed to have received separate orders that, because Zhijie relied on his courage and underestimated the enemy, Wendu was entrusted to restrain him; the army was then halted and not permitted to advance deeply.
translations.idiomatic: He also falsely claimed separate orders that, because Zhijie relied on his courage and underestimated the enemy, Wendu was entrusted to restrain him; the army was halted and not permitted to advance deeply.

sentences.zh: 士卒終日跨馬被甲結陳，不勝疲頓，馬多瘦死。

translations.literal: The soldiers spent entire days mounted, armored, and in formation, utterly exhausted; many horses grew thin and died.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers spent entire days mounted, armored, and in formation until utterly exhausted; many horses grew thin and died.

sentences.zh: 定方言於知節曰：「出師欲以討賊，今乃自守，坐自困敝，若遇賊必敗；

translations.literal: Dingfang said to Zhijie: 'We marched out to attack the enemy, yet now we merely defend ourselves, sitting by while we wear ourselves down — if we meet the enemy we are sure to be defeated;
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang said to Zhijie, 'We marched out to attack the enemy, yet now we merely defend ourselves and wear ourselves down — if we meet the enemy we are sure to be defeated;

sentences.zh: 懦怯如此，何以立功！

translations.literal: to be so timid and cowardly — how can one achieve merit!
translations.idiomatic: to be so timid — how can one achieve merit!

sentences.zh: 且主上以公為大將，豈可更遣軍副專其號令，事必不然。

translations.literal: Moreover, His Majesty appointed you as supreme commander — how could he additionally send a deputy to monopolize your orders? Such a thing cannot be.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, His Majesty appointed you supreme commander — how could he send a deputy to monopolize your orders? Such a thing cannot be.

sentences.zh: 請囚文度，飛表以聞。」

translations.literal: I beg that Wendu be imprisoned and a rapid memorial sent to inform the throne.'
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Wendu be imprisoned and a rapid memorial sent to the throne.'

sentences.zh: 知節不從。

translations.literal: Zhijie did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie did not follow his advice.

sentences.zh: 至恆篤城，有群胡歸附，文度曰「此屬伺我旋師，還復為賊，不如盡殺之，取其資財。」

translations.literal: When they reached Hengdu City, a group of barbarians came to submit. Wendu said: 'These people will wait until we withdraw and then become rebels again — better to kill them all and seize their goods.'
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Hengdu City, a group of barbarians came to submit. Wendu said, 'These people will wait until we withdraw and rebel again — better to kill them all and seize their goods.'

sentences.zh: 定方曰：「如此乃自為賊耳，何名伐叛！」

translations.literal: Dingfang said: 'To do so would make us rebels ourselves — what would be the name of suppressing rebellion!'
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang said, 'To do so would make us rebels ourselves — what would be the name of suppressing rebellion!'

sentences.zh: 文度竟殺之，分其財，獨定方不受。

translations.literal: Wendu ultimately killed them and divided their goods; only Dingfang refused to accept any.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu ultimately killed them and divided their goods; only Dingfang refused any share.

sentences.zh: 師旋，文度坐矯詔當死，特除名；

translations.literal: When the army returned, Wendu was charged with forging an edict, a capital offense; he was specially stripped of his name and office;
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Wendu was charged with forging an edict, a capital offense, and was specially stripped of rank and office;

sentences.zh: 知節亦坐逗遛追賊不及，減死免官。

translations.literal: Zhijie was also charged with dawdling and failing to pursue the enemy, his sentence reduced from death and he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie was also charged with dawdling and failing to pursue the enemy; his sentence was reduced from death and he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 是歲，以太常卿駙馬都尉高履行為益州長史。

translations.literal: That year, Gao Lüxing, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Commandant of Cavalry with imperial marriage ties, was appointed chief administrator of Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Gao Lüxing, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and imperial son-in-law, was appointed chief administrator of Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 韓瑗上疏，為褚遂良訟冤曰：「遂良體國忘家，捐身徇物，風霜其操，鐵石其心，社稷之舊臣，陛下之賢佐。

translations.literal: “Han Yuan submitted a memorial pleading Chu Suiliang's innocence, saying: 'Suiliang embodied the state and forgot his family, gave his person in service to public affairs, his conduct weathered by wind and frost, his heart iron and stone — an old minister of the altars of soil and grain, Your Majesty's worthy assistant.
translations.idiomatic: “Han Yuan submitted a memorial pleading Chu Suiliang's innocence, saying that Suiliang had embodied the state above his family, given himself to public service, borne a conduct weathered by hardship and a heart of iron — an old minister of the realm and the emperor's worthy assistant.

sentences.zh: 無聞罪狀，斥去朝廷，內外□黎，鹹嗟舉措。

translations.literal: No crime was heard of, yet he was expelled from court; within and without, the common people all sighed at this act.
translations.idiomatic: No crime was established, yet he was expelled from court; within and without, the common people all lamented this act.

sentences.zh: 臣聞晉武弘裕，不貽劉毅之誅；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that Emperor Wu of Jin was magnanimous and did not visit the punishment of death upon Liu Yi;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant recalls that Emperor Wu of Jin was magnanimous and did not put Liu Yi to death;

sentences.zh: 漢祖深仁，無恚周昌之直。

translations.literal: the Founding Emperor of Han was deeply benevolent and bore no resentment toward Zhou Chang's bluntness.
translations.idiomatic: and the Founding Emperor of Han was deeply benevolent and bore no resentment toward Zhou Chang's bluntness.

sentences.zh: 而遂良被遷，已經寒暑，違忤陛下，其罰塞焉。

translations.literal: Yet Suiliang has been transferred and has already passed through the seasons; whatever offense against Your Majesty, his punishment is sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Suiliang has been transferred and has already passed through the seasons; whatever offense against Your Majesty, his punishment is surely sufficient.

sentences.zh: 伏願緬鑒無辜，稍寬非罪，俯矜微款，以順人情。」

translations.literal: I humbly beg that Your Majesty look back upon his innocence, slightly ease his undeserved punishment, and condescend to regard this humble plea, so as to accord with human feeling.'"
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg that Your Majesty look back upon his innocence, ease his undeserved punishment, and condescend to this humble plea, so as to accord with the feelings of the people."

sentences.zh: 上謂瑗曰：「遂良之情，朕亦知之。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Yuan: 'I also know Suiliang's feelings.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Yuan, 'I also know Suiliang's feelings.

sentences.zh: 然其悖戾好犯上，故以此責之，卿何言之深也！」

translations.literal: Yet he is perverse and rebellious and fond of offending his superiors; therefore I blame him thus — why do you speak so strongly!'
translations.idiomatic: Yet he is perverse and fond of offending his superiors; therefore I blame him thus — why do you speak so strongly!'

sentences.zh: 對曰：「遂良社稷忠臣，為讒諛所毀。

translations.literal: Yuan replied: 'Suiliang is a loyal minister of the altars of soil and grain, destroyed by slanderers and flatterers.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan replied, 'Suiliang is a loyal minister of the realm, destroyed by slanderers and flatterers.

sentences.zh: 昔微子去而殷國以亡，張華存而綱紀不亂。

translations.literal: Formerly when Weizi departed, the state of Yin perished; when Zhang Hua remained, the laws and institutions were not thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly when Weizi departed, the Yin state perished; when Zhang Hua remained, order was preserved.

sentences.zh: 陛下無故棄逐舊臣，恐非國家之福！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty has cast out an old minister without cause — I fear this is not a blessing for the state!'
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has cast out an old minister without cause — I fear this is not a blessing for the state!'

sentences.zh: 上不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept his advice.

sentences.zh: 瑗以言不用，乞歸田裡，上不許。

translations.literal: Yuan, because his words were not heeded, begged to return to his fields, but the emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, because his advice was not heeded, begged to retire to his fields, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 劉洎之子訟其父冤，稱貞觀之末，為褚遂良所譖而死，李義府復助之。

translations.literal: Liu Ji's son pleaded his father's wrongful death, claiming that at the end of the Zhenguan era his father had been slandered to death by Chu Suiliang, with Li Yifu assisting.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji's son pleaded his father's wrongful death, claiming that at the end of the Zhenguan era his father had been slandered to death by Chu Suiliang with Li Yifu's assistance.

sentences.zh: 上以問近臣，眾希義府之旨，皆言其枉。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned his close ministers; the multitude, hoping to please Yifu's intent, all said the charge was false.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned his close ministers; hoping to please Yifu, they all said the charge was false.

sentences.zh: 給事中長安樂彥瑋獨曰：「劉洎大臣，人主暫有不豫，豈得遽自比伊、霍！

translations.literal: Attending Censor Le Yanyi of Chang'an alone said: 'Liu Ji was a great minister; when the ruler is briefly unwell, how could he abruptly compare himself to Yi Yin and Huo Guang!
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Le Yanyi of Chang'an alone said, 'Liu Ji was a great minister; when the ruler is briefly unwell, how could he abruptly compare himself to Yi Yin and Huo Guang!

sentences.zh: 今雪洎之罪，謂先帝用刑不當乎！」

translations.literal: To clear Ji's guilt now — would that not mean the late emperor used punishment improperly!'
translations.idiomatic: To clear Ji's guilt now — would that not mean the late emperor used punishment improperly!'

sentences.zh: 上然其言，遂寢其事。

translations.literal: The emperor considered his words correct and thereupon shelved the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed with him and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸巳，分哥邏祿部置陰山、大漠二都督府。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on day guisi, the Geluolu division was partitioned and two protectorate headquarters were established at Yinshan and Damo.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on day guisi, the Geluolu were divided and two protectorate headquarters were set up at Yinshan and Damo.

sentences.zh: 閏月，壬寅，上行幸洛陽。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on day renyin, the emperor proceeded in person to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on day renyin, the emperor traveled to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以右屯衛將軍蘇定方為伊麗道行軍總管，帥燕然都護渭南任雅相、副都護蕭嗣業發回紇等兵，自北道討西突厥沙缽羅可汗。

translations.literal: On day gengxu, Su Dingfang, General of the Right Garrison Guards, was made Grand Commander of the Campaign on the Yili Route; commanding the Commandant-in-Chief of the Protectorate General of the Pacified North Ren Yaxiang of Weinan and Deputy Commandant Xiao Siye, he mobilized Uyghur and other troops from the northern route to attack Shaboluo Qaghan of the Western Turks.
translations.idiomatic: On day gengxu, Su Dingfang, general of the Right Garrison Guards, was appointed grand commander of the Yili campaign; leading Protectorate commandant Ren Yaxiang of Weinan and deputy commandant Xiao Siye, he raised Uyghur and allied forces on the northern route to attack the Western Turkic qaghan Shaboluo.

sentences.zh: 嗣業，鉅之子也。

translations.literal: Siye was Ju's son.
translations.idiomatic: Siye was the son of Ju.

sentences.zh: 初，右衛大將軍阿史那彌射及族兄左屯衛大將軍步真，皆西突厥酋長，太宗之世，帥眾來降；

translations.literal: Initially, Right Guard General Ashina Mishe and his clansman Left Garrison Guard General Ashina Buzhen were both chiefs of the Western Turks; in Taizong's time they led their followers to submit;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Right Guard general Ashina Mishe and his clansman Left Garrison Guard general Ashina Buzhen had both been Western Turkic chieftains; in Taizong's reign they led their people to surrender;

sentences.zh: 至是，詔以彌射、步真為流沙安撫大使，自南道招集舊眾。

translations.literal: At this juncture, an edict appointed Mishe and Buzhen Pacification Commissioners of the Flowing Sands, to gather their former followers by the southern route.
translations.idiomatic: At this time an edict named Mishe and Buzhen pacification commissioners of the Flowing Sands, to rally their former followers along the southern route.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛酉，車駕至洛陽宮。

translations.literal: In the second month, on day xinyou, the imperial carriage reached the Luoyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on day xinyou, the imperial procession reached the Luoyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 庚午，立皇子顯為周王。

translations.literal: On day gengwu, the emperor's son Xian was installed as Prince of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: On day gengwu, the emperor's son Xian was installed as Prince of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 壬申，徙雍王素節為郇王。

translations.literal: On day renshen, Prince of Yong Su Jie was transferred to Prince of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: On day renshen, Prince of Yong Su Jie was reassigned as Prince of Xun.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲辰，以潭州都督褚遂良為桂州都督。

translations.literal: In the third month, on day jiachen, Chu Suiliang, Commissioner-in-Chief of Tanzhou, was appointed Commissioner-in-Chief of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on day jiachen, Chu Suiliang was moved from commissioner of Tanzhou to commissioner of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以李義府兼中書令。

translations.literal: On day guichou, Li Yifu was additionally appointed Director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On day guichou, Li Yifu was additionally appointed director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，丙申，上幸明德宮避暑。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on day bingshen, the emperor visited Mingde Palace to escape the heat.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on day bingshen, the emperor went to Mingde Palace to escape the heat.

sentences.zh: 上自即位，每日視事；

translations.literal: Since his accession to the throne, the emperor attended to state affairs every day;
translations.idiomatic: Since his accession, the emperor had attended to state affairs every day;

sentences.zh: 庚子，宰相奏天下無虞，請隔日視事；

translations.literal: On day gengzi, the chief ministers memorialized that the realm was secure and requested that he attend to affairs on alternate days;
translations.idiomatic: On day gengzi, the chief ministers reported that the realm was at peace and asked that he hear business on alternate days;

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: He assented.
translations.idiomatic: He agreed.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁亥朔，上還洛陽宮。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day of the month, day dinghai, the emperor returned to the Luoyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day, day dinghai, the emperor returned to the Luoyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 王玄策之破天竺也，得方士那羅邇娑婆寐以歸，自言有長生之術。

translations.literal: When Wang Xuance conquered India, he brought back the adept Narayana Samadhi, who claimed to possess the art of longevity.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Xuance defeated India, he brought back the adept Narayana Samadhi, who claimed to know the secret of long life.

sentences.zh: 太宗頗信之，深加禮敬，使合長生藥。

translations.literal: Taizong trusted him considerably, treated him with the highest respect, and had him compound a longevity elixir.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong believed him deeply, honored him lavishly, and had him compound an elixir of longevity.

sentences.zh: 發使四方求奇藥異石，又發使詣婆羅門諸國採藥。

translations.literal: Envoys were dispatched to the four quarters to seek rare drugs and exotic stones, and envoys were also sent to the Brahman lands to gather medicinals.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to the four quarters for rare drugs and exotic stones, and others were dispatched to Brahman countries to collect medicinals.

sentences.zh: 其言率皆迂誕無實，苟欲以延歲月，藥竟不就，乃放還。

translations.literal: His talk was for the most part absurd and unfounded, merely aiming to prolong the days; the medicine was ultimately not completed, and he was sent back.
translations.idiomatic: His words were mostly absurd and empty, merely meant to buy time; the medicine was never finished, and he was sent home.

sentences.zh: 上即位，復詣長安，又遣歸。

translations.literal: After the present emperor took the throne, he came again to Chang'an and was again sent away.
translations.idiomatic: After the present emperor took the throne, he came to Chang'an again and was sent away again.

sentences.zh: 玄策時為道王友，辛亥，奏言：「此婆羅門實能合長年藥，自詭必成，今遣歸，可惜失之。」

translations.literal: “Xuance was then Companion to the Prince of Dao; on day xinhai he memorialized, saying: 'This Brahman truly can compound a long-life medicine; he boasts that it will surely succeed — to send him back now would be a regrettable loss.'”
translations.idiomatic: “Xuance was then companion to the Prince of Dao; on day xinhai he memorialized that this Brahman could truly compound a longevity elixir and boasted it would surely succeed — to send him away now would be a regrettable loss.”

sentences.zh: 玄策退，上謂侍臣曰：「自古安有神仙！

translations.literal: Xuance withdrew; the emperor said to his attending ministers: 'Since antiquity has there ever been an immortal!
translations.idiomatic: Xuance withdrew; the emperor said to his attending ministers, "Since antiquity has there ever been an immortal!

sentences.zh: 秦始皇、漢武帝求之，疲弊生民，卒無所成。

translations.literal: Qin Shihuang and Emperor Wu of Han sought them, wearing out the people, and in the end achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang and Emperor Wu of Han sought them, exhausting the people, and in the end achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 果有不死之人，今皆安在！」

translations.literal: If there truly were undying men, where are they all now!'"
translations.idiomatic: If there truly were undying men, where are they all now!"

sentences.zh: 李對曰：「誠如聖言。

translations.literal: Li Ji replied: 'Truly, as Your Sagely Majesty says.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji replied, "Truly, as Your Sagely Majesty says.

sentences.zh: 此婆羅門今茲再來，容發衰白，已改於前，何能長生！

translations.literal: This Brahman has come again now; the hair at his temples has turned white and faded — he has changed from before; how could he achieve longevity!
translations.idiomatic: This Brahman has come again; the hair at his temples has turned white and withered — he is not the man he was before; how could he achieve long life!

sentences.zh: 陛下遣之，內外皆喜。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty's sending him away — within and without the court, all rejoice.'"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's sending him away has pleased everyone inside and outside the court."

sentences.zh: 娑婆寐竟死於長安。

translations.literal: Samadhi ultimately died in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Samadhi ultimately died in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 許敬宗、李義府希皇后旨，誣奏侍中韓瑗、中書令來濟與褚遂良潛謀不軌，以桂州用武之地，授遂良桂州都督，欲以為外援。

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu, hoping to please the empress, falsely memorialized that Attending Secretary Han Yuan and Director of the Central Secretariat Lai Ji had secretly plotted treason with Chu Suiliang — that because Guizhou was a strategic military region, Suiliang was appointed Commissioner of Guizhou to serve as external support.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu, currying favor with the empress, falsely accused Attending Secretary Han Yuan and Central Secretariat director Lai Ji of plotting treason with Chu Suiliang — claiming that because Guizhou was militarily strategic, Suiliang had been made its commissioner to serve as outside support.

sentences.zh: 八月，丁卯，瑗坐貶振州刺史，濟貶台州刺史，終身不聽朝覲。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on day dingmao, Yuan was demoted to Prefect of Zhen, Ji to Prefect of Taizhou, and both were barred from court audiences for life.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on day dingmao, Yuan was demoted to prefect of Zhen and Ji to prefect of Taizhou, and both were barred from court audiences for life.

sentences.zh: 又貶褚遂良為愛州刺史，榮州刺史柳奭為象州刺史。

translations.literal: Chu Suiliang was further demoted to Prefect of Ai, and Prefect of Rong Liu Shang to Prefect of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Suiliang was further demoted to prefect of Ai, and Liu Shang, prefect of Rong, to prefect of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 遂良至愛州，上表自陳：「往者濮王、承乾交爭之際，臣不顧死亡，歸心陛下。

translations.literal: When Suiliang reached Ai Prefecture, he submitted a memorial stating himself: 'In the past, when the Prince of Pu and Chengqian were contending, your servant disregarded death and returned his heart to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: When Suiliang reached Ai Prefecture, he submitted a memorial in his own defense: "In the past, when the Prince of Pu and Chengqian were contending, I disregarded death and gave my heart to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 時岑文本、劉洎奏稱『承乾惡狀已彰，身在別所，其於東宮，不可少時虛曠，請且遣濮王往居東宮。』

translations.literal: At that time Cen Wenti and Liu Ji memorialized that "Chengqian's wicked conduct was already evident; he was dwelling elsewhere — the Eastern Palace must not be left vacant even briefly; please for the time being send the Prince of Pu to reside in the Eastern Palace."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cen Wenti and Liu Ji memorialized that Chengqian's wicked conduct was already clear, that he was living elsewhere, and that the Eastern Palace must not be left vacant even briefly — they asked that the Prince of Pu be sent for the time being to reside in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 臣又抗言固爭，皆陛下所見。

translations.literal: Your servant also spoke out in firm opposition — all of which Your Majesty witnessed.
translations.idiomatic: I also spoke out in firm opposition — all of which Your Majesty witnessed.

sentences.zh: 卒與無忌等四人共定大策。

translations.literal: In the end, together with Wuji and three others, we fixed the great decision.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, together with Wuji and three others, I helped settle the great decision.

sentences.zh: 及先朝大漸，獨臣與無忌同受遺詔。

translations.literal: And when the late emperor grew critically ill, your servant alone with Wuji together received the secret edict.
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor grew critically ill, Wuji and I alone received the secret edict.

sentences.zh: 陛下在草土之辰，不勝哀慟，臣以社稷寬譬，陛下手抱臣頸。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty was still in mourning garments, overcome with grief, your servant with comforting words about the altars of state — Your Majesty clasped your servant about the neck.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty was still in deepest mourning, overcome with grief, I comforted you for the sake of the realm, and Your Majesty clasped my neck in your arms.

sentences.zh: 臣與無忌區處眾事，鹹無廢闕，數日之間，內外寧謐。

translations.literal: Your servant and Wuji arranged all affairs, and nothing was left neglected; within a few days, within and without were tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji and I arranged all affairs without neglect; within a few days, within and without the court were tranquil.

sentences.zh: 力小任重，動罹愆過，螻蟻餘齒，乞陛下哀憐。」

translations.literal: My strength is small yet my burden great; in action I often incur faults — in the remaining days of an ant, I beg Your Majesty's pity.'"
translations.idiomatic: My strength is small yet my burden is great; I often err in action — in the few days left to an ant, I beg Your Majesty's pity."

sentences.zh: 表奏，不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and received no response.

sentences.zh: 己巳，禮官奏：「四郊迎氣，存太微五帝之祀；

translations.literal: “On day jisi, the ritual officials memorialized: 'At the four suburban rites welcoming the seasonal qi, the sacrifices to the Five Emperors of Taiwei should be retained;
translations.idiomatic: “On day jisi, the ritual officials memorialized that at the four suburban rites welcoming the seasonal qi, the sacrifices to the Five Emperors of Taiwei should be retained;

sentences.zh: 南郊明堂，廢緯書六天之義。

translations.literal: at the southern suburb and Bright Hall, the doctrine of the Six Heavens from the weft texts should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: at the southern suburb and Bright Hall, the weft-text doctrine of the Six Heavens should be abolished.

sentences.zh: 其方丘祭地之外，別有神州，亦請合為一祀。」

translations.literal: Apart from the square mound rites to Earth, there is also the Spirit Land — we also request that these be combined into one sacrifice.'"
translations.idiomatic: Apart from the square-mound rites to Earth, there is also the Spirit Land altar — they also asked that these be combined into a single sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以禮部尚書許敬宗為侍中，兼度支尚書杜正倫為兼中書令。

translations.literal: On day xinwei, Xu Jingzong, Minister of Rites, was appointed Attending Secretary; Du Zhenlun, concurrently Minister of Revenue, was appointed concurrently Director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On day xinwei, Xu Jingzong, minister of rites, was made attending secretary, and Du Zhenlun, concurrently minister of revenue, was additionally made director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊戌，上行幸許州。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on day wuxu, the emperor proceeded in person to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on day wuxu, the emperor traveled to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，畋於滍水之南。

translations.literal: On day yisi, he hunted south of the Zhi River.
translations.idiomatic: On day yisi, he hunted south of the Zhi River.

sentences.zh: 壬子，至祀水曲。

translations.literal: On day renzi, he reached the bend of the Si River.
translations.idiomatic: On day renzi, he reached the bend of the Si River.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙卯朔，車駕還洛陽宮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day of the month, day yimao, the imperial carriage returned to the Luoyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the first day, day yimao, the imperial procession returned to the Luoyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 蘇定方擊西突厥沙缽羅可汗，至金山北，先擊處木昆部，大破之，其俟斤懶獨祿等帥萬餘帳來降，定方撫之，發其千騎與俱。

translations.literal: Su Dingfang attacked Shaboluo Qaghan of the Western Turks; reaching north of Gold Mountain, he first struck the Chumukun division and routed it decisively; its yabghu Niduolu and others led more than ten thousand tents to surrender; Dingfang comforted them and sent forth a thousand of their horsemen to march with him.
translations.idiomatic: Su Dingfang attacked the Western Turkic qaghan Shaboluo; reaching north of Gold Mountain, he first struck the Chumukun and routed them; their yabghu Niduolu and others led more than ten thousand tents to surrender; Dingfang received them and took a thousand of their horsemen with him.

sentences.zh: 右領軍郎將薛仁貴上言：「泥孰部素不伏賀魯，為賀魯所破，虜其妻子。

translations.literal: “Right Collegiate Officer Xue Rengui memorialized: 'The Nishu division has never submitted to Helu; Helu destroyed them and seized their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: “Right collegiate officer Xue Rengui memorialized that the Nishu had never submitted to Helu; Helu had destroyed them and seized their wives and children.

sentences.zh: 今唐兵有破賀魯諸部得泥孰妻子者，宜歸之，仍加賜賚，使彼明知賀魯為賊而大唐為之父母，則人致其死，不遺力矣。」

translations.literal: Now wherever Tang forces break Helu's divisions and recover Nishu wives and children, they should be returned and further rewarded, so that they clearly know Helu is the enemy and Great Tang is their parent — then men will give their utmost and spare no effort.'"
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Tang forces defeat Helu's divisions and recover Nishu wives and children, they should be returned and further rewarded, so that they clearly see Helu as the enemy and Great Tang as their protector — then men will give their lives without sparing effort."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 泥孰喜，請從軍共擊賀魯。

translations.literal: The Nishu were pleased and requested to follow the army in a joint attack on Helu.
translations.idiomatic: The Nishu were delighted and asked to join the army in attacking Helu.

sentences.zh: 定方至曳咥河西，沙缽羅帥十姓兵且十萬來拒戰。

translations.literal: When Dingfang reached west of the Yechi River, Shaboluo led nearly one hundred thousand soldiers of the ten surnames to resist in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Dingfang reached west of the Yechi River, Shaboluo led nearly one hundred thousand warriors of the ten surnames to give battle.

sentences.zh: 定方將唐兵及回紇萬餘人擊之。

translations.literal: Dingfang with Tang troops and more than ten thousand Uyghurs struck them.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang led Tang troops and more than ten thousand Uyghurs against them.

sentences.zh: 沙缽羅輕定方兵少，直進圍之。

translations.literal: Shaboluo, underestimating Dingfang's few troops, advanced directly to encircle them.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo, despising Dingfang's small force, advanced straight to encircle him.

sentences.zh: 定方令步兵據南原，攢槊外向，自將騎兵陳於北原。

translations.literal: Dingfang ordered the foot soldiers to hold the southern height, massed spears pointing outward, while he personally arrayed the cavalry on the northern height.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang ordered the infantry to hold the southern height with spears massed pointing outward, while he personally arrayed the cavalry on the northern height.

sentences.zh: 沙缽羅先攻步軍，三沖不動，定方引騎兵擊之，沙缽羅大敗，追奔三十里，斬獲數萬人；

translations.literal: Shaboluo first attacked the foot soldiers; three charges failed to move them; Dingfang led the cavalry to strike, and Shaboluo was utterly defeated; pursued for thirty li, tens of thousands were slain or captured;
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo attacked the infantry first; three charges failed to budge them; Dingfang led the cavalry in and routed Shaboluo utterly; pursued thirty li, slaying and capturing tens of thousands;

sentences.zh: 明日，勒兵復進。

translations.literal: The next day, he arrayed the troops and advanced again.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he reformed the army and advanced again.

sentences.zh: 於是胡祿屋等五弩失畢悉眾來降，沙缽羅獨與處木昆屈律啜數百騎西走。

translations.literal: Thereupon the five Nushibi of Huluwu and the rest all came leading their masses to surrender; Shaboluo alone with Qulüchu of Chumukun and several hundred horsemen fled west.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the five Nushibi led by Huluwu all came over with their full strength; Shaboluo alone fled west with Qulüchu of Chumukun and a few hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 時阿史那步真出南道，五咄陸部落聞沙缽羅敗，皆詣步真降。

translations.literal: At that time Ashina Buzhen had come out by the southern route; hearing of Shaboluo's defeat, all the Wudulu tribes came to Buzhen to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ashina Buzhen was advancing on the southern route; hearing of Shaboluo's defeat, all the Wudulu tribes came to Buzhen to surrender.

sentences.zh: 定方乃命蕭嗣業、回紇婆閏將胡兵趨邪羅斯川，追沙缽羅，定方與任雅相將新附之眾繼之。

translations.literal: Dingfang then ordered Xiao Siye and the Uyghur Bogul Khan to lead the Turkic troops toward the Talas River in pursuit of Shaboluo; Dingfang with Ren Yaxiang led the newly submitted masses to follow after.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang then ordered Xiao Siye and the Uyghur Bogul Khan to lead Turkic troops toward the Talas River in pursuit of Shaboluo, while he and Ren Yaxiang followed with the newly submitted forces.

sentences.zh: 會大雪，平地二尺，軍中鹹請俟晴而行，定方曰：「虜恃雪深，謂我不能進，必休息士馬。

translations.literal: Heavy snow fell, two chi deep on level ground; throughout the army they all requested to wait for clear weather before marching; Dingfang said: 'The enemy relies on the deep snow, thinking we cannot advance — they will surely rest men and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow fell, two feet deep on level ground; the whole army asked to wait for clear weather; Dingfang said, "The enemy will rely on the deep snow, thinking we cannot advance, and will surely rest their men and horses.

sentences.zh: 亟追之可及，若緩之，彼遁逃浸遠，不可復追，省日兼功，在此時矣！」

translations.literal: Pursue them swiftly and we can overtake them; if we delay, they will slip away ever farther and cannot be pursued again — sparing days while doubling achievement lies in this moment!'"
translations.idiomatic: Pursue them swiftly and we can catch them; if we delay, they will slip farther away and cannot be pursued — to save time and double our gains, the moment is now!"

sentences.zh: 乃蹋雪晝夜兼行，所過收其部眾，至雙河，與彌射、步真兵合，去沙缽羅所居二百里，布陳長驅，逕至其牙帳。

translations.literal: Thereupon they trampled through snow by day and night in forced marches, gathering tribal followers as they passed; reaching Shuanghe, they united with Mishe and Buzhen's troops; two hundred li from where Shaboluo dwelt, they deployed their arrays and drove forward directly to his imperial tent.
translations.idiomatic: They then marched day and night through the snow, gathering tribal followers as they went; at Shuanghe they joined Mishe and Buzhen's forces; two hundred li from Shaboluo's camp they deployed and drove straight to his royal tent.

sentences.zh: 沙缽羅與其徒將獵，定方掩其不備，縱兵擊之，斬獲數萬人，得其鼓纛，沙缽羅與其子咥運、婿閻啜等脫走，趣石國。

translations.literal: Shaboluo with his followers was out hunting; Dingfang took him unawares and unleashed his troops; tens of thousands were slain or captured, and his drums and banners were taken; Shaboluo with his son Niyun, son-in-law Yanchuo, and others escaped, hastening toward the Stone Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo and his followers were out hunting; Dingfang took them unawares and attacked; tens of thousands were slain or captured and his drums and banners were seized; Shaboluo escaped with his son Niyun, son-in-law Yanchuo, and others, fleeing toward the Stone Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 定方於是息兵，諸部各歸所居，通道路，置郵驛，掩骸骨，問疾苦，畫疆場，復生業，凡為沙缽羅所掠者，悉括還之，十姓安堵如故。

translations.literal: Dingfang then rested the troops; each division returned to its dwelling; roads were opened, post stations set, bones covered, hardships inquired after, borders drawn, livelihoods restored — all that Shaboluo had plundered was fully returned; the ten surnames were settled as before.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang then rested the army; each tribe returned to its home; roads were opened, post stations established, the dead buried, the afflicted comforted, borders marked, and livelihoods restored — everything Shaboluo had plundered was returned, and the ten surnames were settled as before.

sentences.zh: 乃命蕭嗣業將兵追沙缽羅，定方引軍還。

translations.literal: He then ordered Xiao Siye to lead troops in pursuit of Shaboluo while Dingfang led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Xiao Siye to pursue Shaboluo while Dingfang led the army back.

sentences.zh: 沙缽羅至石國西北蘇咄城，人馬饑乏，遣人繼珍寶入城市馬。

translations.literal: Shaboluo reached Sudu City northwest of the Stone Kingdom; men and horses were famished and exhausted; he sent men bearing jewels and treasures into the city to buy horses.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo reached Sudu City northwest of the Stone Kingdom; his men and horses were starving and exhausted; he sent men with jewels and treasures into the city to buy horses.

sentences.zh: 城主伊沮達官詐以酒食出迎，誘之入，閉門執之，送於石國。

translations.literal: The city lord, chieftain Yijuda, feigned welcome with wine and food, lured him in, closed the gate and seized him, and sent him to the Stone Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: The city lord Yijuda feigned welcome with food and wine, lured him inside, closed the gates and seized him, and handed him over to the Stone Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 蕭嗣業至石國，石國人以沙缽羅授之。

translations.literal: When Xiao Siye reached the Stone Kingdom, the people of the Stone Kingdom handed Shaboluo over to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Siye reached the Stone Kingdom, its people handed Shaboluo over to him.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，分西突厥地置濛池、昆陵二都護府，以阿史那彌射為左衛大將軍、昆陵都護、興昔亡可汗，押五咄陸部落；

translations.literal: On day yichou, the Western Turkic lands were divided and two Protectorates General were established at Mengchi and Kunling — Ashina Mishe as General-in-Chief of the Left Guard, Protector General of Kunling, and Khan Reviving the Past Xingxiwang, overseeing the Wudulu tribes;
translations.idiomatic: On day yichou, the Western Turkic lands were divided and two protectorates general were set up at Mengchi and Kunling — Ashina Mishe was made general-in-chief of the Left Guard, protector general of Kunling, and khan Reviving the Past, overseeing the Wudulu tribes;

sentences.zh: 阿史那步真為右衛大將軍、濛池都護、繼往絕可汗，押五弩失畢部落。

translations.literal: Ashina Buzhen as General-in-Chief of the Right Guard, Protector General of Mengchi, and Khan Continuing the Past Jiwangjue, overseeing the Wunushi tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Buzhen was made general-in-chief of the Right Guard, protector general of Mengchi, and khan Continuing the Past, overseeing the Wunushi tribes.

sentences.zh: 遣光祿卿盧承慶持節冊命，仍命彌射、步真與承慶據諸姓降者，准其部落大小，位望高下，授刺史以下官。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Household Lu Chengqing was dispatched bearing credentials to invest them; Mishe and Buzhen were also ordered with Chengqing, according to those of various surnames who had surrendered, to grant offices from prefect downward commensurate with each tribe's size and each man's standing.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Household Lu Chengqing was sent with credentials to invest them; Mishe and Buzhen were also ordered, together with Chengqing, to grant offices down to prefect according to the size of each surrendered tribe and each man's standing.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以洛陽宮為東都，洛州官吏員品並如雍州。

translations.literal: On day dingmao, the Luoyang Palace was made the Eastern Capital; the staff ranks and offices of Luozhou were made identical to those of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On day dingmao, the Luoyang Palace was made the Eastern Capital, and Luozhou's official ranks and posts were made identical to Yongzhou's.

sentences.zh: 是歲，詔：「自今僧尼不得受父母及尊者禮拜，所司明有法制禁斷。」

translations.literal: “That year, an edict: 'Henceforth monks and nuns must not receive obeisance from parents and elders; the relevant offices are clearly to enforce prohibition by statute.'”
translations.idiomatic: “That year an edict declared that henceforth monks and nuns must not receive obeisance from parents and elders, and that the relevant offices were to enforce the prohibition by law.”
translations.footnote: Closing quotation mark in the source

sentences.zh: 以吏部侍郎劉祥道為黃門侍郎，仍知吏部選事。

translations.literal: Liu Xiangdao, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, was appointed Vice Minister of the Huangmen; he continued to oversee personnel selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiangdao, vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel, was appointed vice minister of the Huangmen and continued to oversee personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 祥道以為：「今選司取士傷濫，每年入流之數，過一千四百，雜色入流，曾不銓簡。

translations.literal: “Xiangdao held: 'The selection office today recruits scholars with excessive laxity; the annual number entering the flow ranks exceeds fourteen hundred, and miscellaneous entrants into the flow are never screened or winnowed.
translations.idiomatic: “Xiangdao argued that the selection office was recruiting too loosely: more than fourteen hundred people entered the flow ranks each year, and miscellaneous entrants were never screened.

sentences.zh: 即日內外文武官一品至九品，凡萬三千四百六十五員，約准三十年，則萬三千餘人略盡矣。

translations.literal: At present civil and military officials within and without, from first to ninth rank, total thirteen thousand four hundred sixty-five posts; roughly projected over thirty years, these thirteen-odd thousand would be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: At present there were thirteen thousand four hundred sixty-five civil and military posts from first to ninth rank; projected over thirty years, those thirteen-odd thousand posts would be filled.

sentences.zh: 若年別入流者五百人，足充所須之數。

translations.literal: If five hundred entered the flow ranks each year, that would suffice for what is needed.
translations.idiomatic: If only five hundred entered the flow ranks each year, that would meet the state's needs.

sentences.zh: 望有釐革。」

translations.literal: I hope there may be rectification and reform.'"
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the system be reformed."

sentences.zh: 既而杜正倫亦言入流人太多。

translations.literal: Thereupon Du Zhenglun also said that those entering the flow were too numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhenglun also said that too many people were entering the flow ranks.

sentences.zh: 上命正倫與祥道詳議，而大臣憚於改作，事遂寢。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zhenglun and Xiangdao to deliberate in detail, but the great ministers shrank from reform, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zhenglun and Xiangdao to discuss the matter in detail, but the senior ministers shrank from reform and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 祥道，杜甫之子也。

translations.literal: Xiangdao was a son of Du Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangdao was a son of the poet Du Fu.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊子，長孫無忌等上所修新禮；

translations.literal: In spring, first month, day wuzi, Zhangsun Wuji and others presented the newly compiled rites to the emperor;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on day wuzi, Zhangsun Wuji and others presented the newly compiled rites to the emperor;

sentences.zh: 詔中外行之。

translations.literal: an edict ordered them implemented throughout the court and realm.
translations.idiomatic: and an edict ordered them implemented throughout the court and realm.

sentences.zh: 先是，議者謂貞觀禮節文未備，故命無忌等修之。

translations.literal: Previously, critics had held that the Zhenguan ritual corpus was incomplete in text and detail, and the emperor had therefore ordered Wuji and others to revise it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, critics had said the Zhenguan ritual corpus was incomplete, and the emperor had ordered Wuji and others to revise it.

sentences.zh: 時許敬宗、李義府用事，所損益多希旨，學者非之。

translations.literal: At the time Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu held power; most additions and deletions curried favor, and scholars decried them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu held power; most changes curried favor with the throne, and scholars criticized the result.

sentences.zh: 太常博士蕭楚材等以為豫備凶事，非臣子所宜言；

translations.literal: Directors of Studies at the Chamber of Rites Xiao Chucai and others held that to prepare for unlucky affairs in advance was not language fit for subjects;
translations.idiomatic: Directors of studies at the Chamber of Rites, Xiao Chucai and others, argued that to prepare for funeral rites in advance was not language fit for subjects;

sentences.zh: 敬宗、義府深然之，遂焚《國恤》一篇，由是凶禮遂闕。

translations.literal: Jingzong and Yifu strongly agreed; they then burned the chapter 'National Mourning' of the rites, and thus funeral rites were left defective.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong and Yifu strongly agreed; they burned the chapter on national mourning, and funeral rites were thereby left incomplete.

sentences.zh: 初，龜茲王布失畢妻阿史那氏與其相那利私通，布失畢不能禁，由是君臣猜阻，各有黨與，互來告難。

translations.literal: Earlier, Kucha king Bu Shibi's wife, of the Ashina clan, had an affair with his minister Nali; Bu Shibi could not restrain it; hence ruler and minister grew mutually suspicious, each with factions, repeatedly accusing one another.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Kucha king Bu Shibi's wife, of the Ashina clan, had an affair with his minister Nali, which Bu Shibi could not stop; ruler and minister grew suspicious of each other, each gathered supporters, and they repeatedly denounced one another to the court.

sentences.zh: 上兩召之，既至，囚那利，遣左領軍郎將雷文成送布失畢歸國。

translations.literal: The emperor twice summoned them; once they arrived, he imprisoned Nali and sent Left Army Guard commandant Lei Wencheng to escort Bu Shibi back to his kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned them twice; when they arrived he imprisoned Nali and sent Left Army Guard commandant Lei Wencheng to escort Bu Shibi home.

sentences.zh: 至龜茲東境泥師城，龜茲大將羯獵顛發眾拒之，仍遣使降於西突厥沙缽羅可汗。

translations.literal: At Nishi city on Kucha's eastern border, Kucha general Jieliedian raised troops to resist and also sent envoys to surrender to Western Turkic khan Shaboluo.
translations.idiomatic: At Nishi city on Kucha's eastern border, the Kucha general Jieliedian raised troops to resist and also sent envoys to surrender to the Western Turkic khan Shaboluo.

sentences.zh: 布失畢據城自守，不敢進。

translations.literal: Bu Shibi held the city and defended himself, not daring to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Shibi held the city and would not advance.

sentences.zh: 詔左屯衛大將軍楊冑發兵討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Left Garrison Guard general-in-chief Yang Zhou to raise troops and subdue him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Left Garrison Guard general-in-chief Yang Zhou to raise troops and suppress the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 會布失畢病卒，冑與羯獵顛戰，大破之，擒羯獵顛及其黨，盡誅之，乃以其地為龜茲都督府。

translations.literal: Bu Shibi happened to die of illness; Zhou fought Jieliedian and routed him utterly, capturing Jieliedian and his faction and executing them all; the territory was then made the Kucha Protectorate Command.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Shibi died of illness; Zhou fought Jieliedian, routed him, captured Jieliedian and his followers and executed them all, and the territory was made the Kucha Protectorate Command.

sentences.zh: 戊申，立布失畢之子素稽為龜茲王兼都督。

translations.literal: On day wushen, Bu Shibi's son Suoji was installed as king of Kucha and concurrently as protector-commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On day wushen, Bu Shibi's son Suoji was installed as king of Kucha and concurrently as protector-commandant.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁巳，上發東都；

translations.literal: Second month, day dingsi, the emperor departed the Eastern Capital;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on day dingsi, the emperor left the Eastern Capital;

sentences.zh: 甲戌，至京師。

translations.literal: on day jiaxu he reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: on day jiaxu he reached the capital.
