sentences.zh: 夏，五月，癸未，徙安西都護府於龜茲，以舊安西夏為西州都督府，鎮高昌故地。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month, day guimwei, the Anxi Protectorate was moved to Kucha; the former Anxi summer quarter became the Xizhou Protectorate Command, garrisoning the old Gaochang territory.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on day guimwei, the Anxi Protectorate was moved to Kucha; the former Anxi summer headquarters became the Xizhou Protectorate Command, garrisoning the old Gaochang territory.

sentences.zh: 六月，營州都督兼東夷都護程名振、右領軍中郎將薛仁貴將兵攻高麗之赤烽鎮，拔之，斬首四百餘級，捕虜百餘人。

translations.literal: Sixth month, Yingzhou Protector and concurrent Eastern Yi Grand Protector Cheng Mingzhen and Right Army Guard mid-ranking general Xue Rengui led troops against Goryeo's Chifeng garrison, took it, beheaded over four hundred, captured over a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Yingzhou protector and concurrent Eastern Yi grand protector Cheng Mingzhen and Right Army Guard mid-ranking general Xue Rengui attacked Goryeo's Chifeng garrison, took it, beheaded more than four hundred, and captured more than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 高麗遣其大將豆方婁帥眾三萬拒之，名振以契丹逆擊，大破之，斬首二千五百級。

translations.literal: Goryeo sent its general Dou Fanglou leading thirty thousand to resist; Mingzhen struck them with Khitan auxiliaries in a counterattack and routed them utterly, beheading twenty-five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo sent its general Dou Fanglou with thirty thousand men to resist; Mingzhen counterattacked with Khitan auxiliaries, routed them, and beheaded twenty-five hundred.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，甲寅，播羅哀獠酋長多胡桑等帥眾內附。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, day jiayin, the Boluo Ai Liao chieftain Duohusang and others led their people to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on day jiayin, the Boluo Ai Liao chieftain Duohusang and others led their people to submit to the court.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，庚申，吐蕃贊普來請婚。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day gengshen, the Tibetan tsenpo came requesting a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on day gengshen, the Tibetan tsenpo came to request a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 中書令李義府有寵於上，諸子孩抱者並列清貴。

translations.literal: Chief Secretariat Counsellor Li Yifu enjoyed the emperor's favor; even his infant sons in arms were ranked among the pure and exalted offices.
translations.idiomatic: Chief secretariat counsellor Li Yifu enjoyed the emperor's favor; even his infant sons in arms held exalted offices.

sentences.zh: 而義府貪冒無厭，母、妻及諸子、女婿，賣官鬻獄，其門如市，多樹朋黨，傾動朝野。

translations.literal: Yet Yifu was grasping and insatiable — his mother, wife, sons, and sons-in-law sold offices and trafficked in legal judgments; his gate was like a marketplace; he planted many factional ties and shook court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yifu was insatiably greedy: his mother, wife, sons, and sons-in-law sold offices and trafficked in legal judgments; his gate was like a marketplace; he built a wide faction and shook court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 中書令杜正倫每以先進自處，義府恃恩，不為之下，由是有隙，與義府訟於上前。

translations.literal: Chief Secretariat Counsellor Du Zhenglun constantly placed himself as a senior pioneer; Yifu relied on favor and would not yield beneath him; thereby a rift arose, and they quarreled before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Chief secretariat counsellor Du Zhenglun treated himself as the senior statesman; Yifu relied on imperial favor and would not defer to him; a rift opened, and they quarreled before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上以大臣不和，兩責之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the great ministers were not harmonious, reproved them both.
translations.idiomatic: Because the great ministers were at odds, the emperor reproved them both.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙酉，貶正倫橫州刺史，義府普州刺史。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day yiyou, Zhenglun was demoted to prefect of Hengzhou, Yifu to prefect of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on day yiyou, Zhenglun was demoted to prefect of Hengzhou and Yifu to prefect of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 正倫尋卒於橫州。

translations.literal: Zhenglun soon died at Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglun soon died at Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 阿史那賀魯既被擒，謂蕭嗣業曰：「我本亡虜，為先帝所存，先帝遇我厚而我負之，今日之敗，天所怒也。

translations.literal: Ashina Helu, having been captured, said to Xiao Siye: 'I was originally a fugitive captive whom the late emperor preserved; the late emperor treated me generously yet I betrayed him — today's defeat is heaven's wrath.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Helu, having been captured, said to Xiao Siye, "I was a fugitive whom the late emperor spared; he treated me generously and I betrayed him — today's defeat is heaven's anger.

sentences.zh: 吾聞中國刑人必於市，願刑我於昭陵之前以謝先帝。」

translations.literal: I have heard that in China criminals are executed in the market; I wish to be executed before Zhaoling to make amends to the late emperor.'"
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that in China criminals are executed in the market; I ask to be executed before Zhaoling to atone to the late emperor."

sentences.zh: 上聞而憐之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this he pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this he pitied him.

sentences.zh: 賀魯至京師，甲午，獻於昭陵。

translations.literal: Helu reached the capital; on day jiawu he was presented at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Helu reached the capital; on day jiawu he was presented at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 敕免其死，分其種落為六都督府，其所役屬諸國皆置州府，西盡波斯，並隸安西都護府。

translations.literal: An edict spared his life; his tribal followers were divided into six protector-commandant prefectures; all subject states under his rule were given prefectures and districts; west as far as Persia, all were placed under the Anxi Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict spared his life; his tribes were divided into six protector-commandant prefectures; all subject states under his rule were given prefectures and districts; west as far as Persia, all were placed under the Anxi Protectorate.

sentences.zh: 賀魯尋死，葬於頡利墓側。

translations.literal: Helu soon died and was buried beside Jieli's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Helu soon died and was buried beside Jieli's tomb.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以許敬宗為中書令，大理卿辛茂將為兼侍中。

translations.literal: On day wuxu, Xu Jingzong was made chief secretariat counsellor, Grand Court of Justice chief Xin Maochan was made concurrent vice-head of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On day wuxu, Xu Jingzong was made chief secretariat counsellor and Grand Court of Justice chief Xin Maochan was made concurrent vice-head of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同三司鄂忠武公尉遲敬德薨。

translations.literal: Minister of State with the Rites of the Equal Third Rank, Duke of E and Loyal Martial, Yuchi Jingde, died.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of state with the rites of the equal third rank, Duke of E and Loyal Martial Yuchi Jingde, died.

sentences.zh: 敬德晚年閒居，學延年術，修飾池台，奏清商樂以自奉養，不交通賓客，凡十六年。

translations.literal: In his later years Jingde lived in retirement, studied longevity arts, adorned pools and terraces, played qingshang music for his own sustenance, and did not socialize with guests — for sixteen years in all.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Jingde lived in retirement, studied longevity arts, adorned his pools and terraces, played qingshang music for his own pleasure, and did not receive guests — for sixteen years in all.

sentences.zh: 年七十四，以病終，朝廷恩禮甚厚。

translations.literal: At seventy-four he died of illness; the court's favors and rites were exceedingly generous.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness at seventy-four, and the court's honors and rites were exceedingly generous.

sentences.zh: 是歲，愛州刺史褚遂良卒。

translations.literal: That year, Prefect of Ai Zhou Chu Suiliang died.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Ai prefecture prefect Chu Suiliang died.

sentences.zh: 雍州司士許禕與來濟善，侍御史張倫與李義府有怨，吏部尚書唐臨奏以禕為江南道巡察使，倫為劍南道巡察使。

translations.literal: Yongzhou judicial officer Xu Yi was friendly with Lai Ji; investigating censor Zhang Lun bore a grudge against Li Yifu; Ministry of Personnel Director Tang Lin memorialized to make Yi inspector of the Jiangnan circuit and Lun inspector of the Jiannan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhou judicial officer Xu Yi was friendly with Lai Ji; investigating censor Zhang Lun bore a grudge against Li Yifu; Ministry of Personnel director Tang Lin memorialized to make Yi inspector of the Jiangnan circuit and Lun inspector of the Jiannan circuit.

sentences.zh: 是時義府雖在外，皇后常保護之。

translations.literal: At this time, though Yifu was in exile, the empress constantly shielded him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yifu was in exile, the empress constantly shielded him.

sentences.zh: 以臨為挾私選授。

translations.literal: Tang Lin was deemed to have made partisan appointments out of private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Lin was charged with making partisan appointments out of private favor.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，乙丑，免臨官。

translations.literal: Spring, second month, day yichou, Lin was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, on day yichou, Tang Lin was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬午，西突厥興昔亡可汗與真珠葉護戰於雙河，斬真珠葉護。

translations.literal: Third month, day renwu, Western Turkic khan Reviving the Past Xingxiwang fought Pearl Protector Zhenzhu at Shuanghe and beheaded Zhenzhu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on day renwu, the Western Turkic khan Reviving the Past fought Pearl Protector Zhenzhu at Shuanghe and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙辰，以於志寧為太子太師、同中書門下三品；

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day bingchen, Yu Zhining was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Fellow of the Secretariat with the Third Rank;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on day bingchen, Yu Zhining was made grand tutor of the heir apparent and fellow of the Secretariat with the third rank;

sentences.zh: 乙丑，以黃門侍郎許圉師參知政事。

translations.literal: on day yichou, Huangmen Vice Minister Xu Yuanshi was made participant in governance.
translations.idiomatic: on day yichou, Huangmen vice minister Xu Yuanshi was made participant in governance.

sentences.zh: 武后以太尉趙公長孫無忌受重賜而不助己，深怨之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu deeply resented Grand Mentor Zhao Duke Zhangsun Wuji because, though he had received heavy rewards, he had not aided her.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu deeply resented Grand Mentor Zhao Duke Zhangsun Wuji because, though he had received heavy rewards, he had not helped her.

sentences.zh: 及議廢王后，燕公於志寧中立不言，武后亦不悅。

translations.literal: When the discussion arose to depose the former empress, Yan Duke Yu Zhining had stood neutral and said nothing — the empress was displeased with him as well.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated deposing the former empress, Yan Duke Yu Zhining had stood neutral and said nothing, and the empress was displeased with him as well.

sentences.zh: 許敬宗屢以利害說無忌，無忌每面折之，敬宗亦怨。

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong repeatedly argued profit and loss to Wuji; Wuji each time rebuked him to his face; Jingzong bore resentment too.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong repeatedly argued the stakes to Wuji; Wuji rebuked him to his face each time, and Jingzong bore a grudge as well.

sentences.zh: 武后既立，無忌內不自安，后令敬宗伺其隙而陷之。

translations.literal: Once Wu was established as empress, Wuji was uneasy within; the empress ordered Jingzong to watch for openings and entrap him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wu was established as empress, Wuji was uneasy within; the empress ordered Jingzong to watch for an opening and entrap him.

sentences.zh: 會洛陽人李奉節告太子洗馬韋季方、監察御史李巢朋黨事，敕敬宗與辛茂將鞫之。

translations.literal: It happened that Luoyang man Li Fengjie reported that heir-apparent study attendant Wei Jifang and investigating censor Li Chao were a faction; an edict ordered Jingzong and Xin Maochan to interrogate.
translations.idiomatic: A Luoyang man named Li Fengjie reported that heir-apparent study attendant Wei Jifang and investigating censor Li Chao were a faction; the emperor ordered Jingzong and Xin Maochan to interrogate them.

sentences.zh: 敬宗按之急，季方自刺，不死，敬宗因誣奏季方欲與無忌構陷忠臣近戚，使權歸無忌，伺隙謀反，今事覺，故自殺。

translations.literal: Jingzong pressed the inquiry harshly; Jifang stabbed himself but did not die; Jingzong then falsely memorialized that Jifang had meant with Wuji to fabricate charges against loyal ministers and imperial kin, concentrate power in Wuji, watch for openings to rebel — now the affair was exposed, hence the suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong pressed the inquiry harshly; Jifang stabbed himself but did not die; Jingzong then falsely memorialized that Jifang had plotted with Wuji to frame loyal ministers and imperial kin, concentrate power in Wuji, and watch for a chance to rebel — now the plot was exposed, hence the suicide attempt.

sentences.zh: 上驚曰：「豈有此邪！

translations.literal: The emperor said in alarm: 'How can there be such a thing!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said in alarm, "How can there be such a thing!

sentences.zh: 舅為小人所間，小生疑阻則有之，何至於反！」

translations.literal: The uncle-in-law may have been set at odds by petty men; petty doubts and hesitations perhaps — how could it reach rebellion!'
translations.idiomatic: My uncle-in-law may have been set at odds by petty men; small doubts and hesitations perhaps — how could it come to rebellion!"

sentences.zh: 敬宗曰：「臣始末推究，反狀已露，陛下猶以為疑，恐非社稷之福。」

translations.literal: Jingzong said: 'Your servant has traced the matter from start to finish; signs of rebellion already show; yet Your Majesty still doubts — I fear that is no blessing to the altars of state.'
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong said, "Your servant has traced the matter from start to finish; signs of rebellion already show; yet Your Majesty still doubts — I fear that is no blessing to the altars of state."

sentences.zh: 上泣曰「我家不幸，親戚間屢有異志，往年高陽公主與房遺愛謀反，今元舅復然，使朕慚見天下之人。

translations.literal: The emperor wept: 'Our house is unlucky; among kin disloyal intent has erupted again and again — years ago Princess Gaoyang and Fang Yi'ai plotted rebellion; now the chief maternal uncle does the same, shaming me before all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept, "Our house is unlucky; among kin disloyal intent has erupted again and again — years ago Princess Gaoyang and Fang Yi'ai plotted rebellion; now the chief maternal uncle does the same, shaming me before all under heaven.

sentences.zh: 茲事若實，如之何？」

translations.literal: If this affair is real, what can be done?'
translations.idiomatic: If this affair is real, what can be done?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「遺愛乳臭兒，與一女子謀反，勢何所成！

translations.literal: He replied: 'Yi'ai was a suckling brat plotting rebellion with a single woman — what force could he muster!
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Yi'ai was a suckling brat plotting rebellion with a single woman — what force could he muster!

sentences.zh: 無忌與先帝謀取天下，天下服其智；

translations.literal: Wuji schemed with the late emperor to win the realm; all under heaven bow to his wits;
translations.idiomatic: Wuji schemed with the late emperor to win the realm; all under heaven bow to his wits;

sentences.zh: 為宰相三十年，天下畏其威；

translations.literal: he was chief minister thirty years; all under heaven fear his might;
translations.idiomatic: he was chief minister for thirty years; all under heaven fear his might;

sentences.zh: 若一旦竊發，陛下遣誰當之？

translations.literal: if he should rise in secret one morning, whom would Your Majesty send to face him?
translations.idiomatic: if he should rise in secret one morning, whom would Your Majesty send to face him?

sentences.zh: 今賴宗廟之靈，皇天疾惡，因按小事，乃得大奸，實天下之慶也。

translations.literal: Now, relying on the ancestral temples' spirit and heaven's hatred of evil, through scrutiny of a small matter we have caught a great traitor — truly the realm's rejoicing.
translations.idiomatic: Now, relying on the ancestral temples' spirit and heaven's hatred of evil, through scrutiny of a small matter we have caught a great traitor — truly the realm's rejoicing.

sentences.zh: 臣竊恐無忌知季方自刺，窘急發謀，攘袂一呼，同惡雲集，必為宗廟之憂。

translations.literal: Your servant privately fears Wuji, learning Jifang stabbed himself, may in desperate straits launch his plot — shake his sleeves and cry once, and fellow evildoers will gather like clouds, surely a worry for the ancestral altars.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant privately fears that if Wuji learns Jifang stabbed himself, he may launch his plot in desperation — shake his sleeves and cry once, and fellow evildoers will gather like clouds, surely a worry for the ancestral altars.

sentences.zh: 臣昔見宇文化及父述為煬帝所親任，結以昏煙，委以朝政；

translations.literal: Your servant once saw Yuwen Huaji's father Shu favored and entrusted by Emperor Yang, allied by marriage, entrusted with court governance;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant once saw Yuwen Huaji's father Shu favored and entrusted by Emperor Yang, allied by marriage, and entrusted with court governance;

sentences.zh: 述卒，化及復典禁兵，一夕於江都作亂，先殺不附己者，臣家亦豫其禍，於是大臣蘇威、裴矩之徒，皆舞蹈馬首，唯恐不及，黎明遂傾隋室。

translations.literal: when Shu died, Huaji again held the forbidden guards; one night at Jiangdu he rebelled, first killing those who would not follow; your servant's household also suffered in that disaster — then great ministers Su Wei, Pei Ju, and the like all danced at his horse's head, fearing to lag; by dawn the Sui house was overturned.
translations.idiomatic: when Shu died, Huaji again held the forbidden guards; one night at Jiangdu he rebelled, first killing those who would not follow; your servant's household also suffered in that disaster — then great ministers Su Wei, Pei Ju, and the like all danced at his horse's head, fearing to lag behind; by dawn the Sui house was overturned.

sentences.zh: 前事不遠，願陛下速決之！」

translations.literal: The recent precedent is not far — I beg Your Majesty to decide swiftly!'
translations.idiomatic: The recent precedent is not far — I beg Your Majesty to decide swiftly!"

sentences.zh: 上命敬宗更加審察。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Jingzong to examine further still.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Jingzong to investigate further.

sentences.zh: 明日，敬宗復奏曰：「去夜季方已承與無忌同反，臣又問季方：『無忌與國至親，累朝寵任，何恨而反？』

translations.literal: The next day Jingzong memorialized again: 'Last night Jifang already confessed conspiracy with Wuji; your servant again asked Jifang: "Wuji is the state's closest kin, favored through successive reigns — what grudge could move him to rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day Jingzong memorialized again: "Last night Jifang already confessed conspiracy with Wuji; your servant again asked Jifang, 'Wuji is the state's closest kin, favored through successive reigns — what grudge could move him to rebel?'

sentences.zh: 季方答云：『韓瑗嘗語無忌云：「柳奭、褚遂良勸公立梁王為太子，今梁王既廢，上亦疑公，故出高履行於外。」

translations.literal: Jifang answered: "Han Yuan once said to Wuji: 'Liu Shi and Chu Suiliang urged Your Grace to install Prince Liang as heir; now Prince Liang is deposed and the emperor also suspects you, hence Gao Lixing was sent out.'
translations.idiomatic: Jifang answered, 'Han Yuan once said to Wuji, "Liu Shi and Chu Suiliang urged you to install Prince Liang as heir; now Prince Liang is deposed and the emperor also suspects you, hence Gao Lixing was sent out."

sentences.zh: 自此無忌憂恐，漸為自安之計。

translations.literal: From this Wuji grew fearful and anxious, gradually making plans to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: From this Wuji grew fearful and anxious and gradually made plans to secure himself.

sentences.zh: 後見長孫祥又出，韓瑗得罪，日夜與季方等謀反。』

translations.literal: Later he saw Zhangsun Xiang also sent out, and Han Yuan punished — day and night he plotted rebellion with Jifang and others.'"
translations.idiomatic: Later he saw Zhangsun Xiang also sent out and Han Yuan punished — day and night he plotted rebellion with Jifang and others.'

sentences.zh: 臣參驗辭狀，鹹相符合，請收捕准法。」

translations.literal: Your servant cross-checked the testimony and statements — all accord; I request arrest according to law.'
translations.idiomatic: Your servant cross-checked the testimony and statements and found them all consistent; I request arrest according to law."

sentences.zh: 上又泣曰：「舅若果爾，朕決不忍殺之；

translations.literal: The emperor again wept: 'If the uncle-in-law is truly so, I absolutely cannot bear to kill him;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again wept, "If my uncle-in-law is truly so, I absolutely cannot bear to kill him;

sentences.zh: 若果殺之，天下將謂朕何！

translations.literal: if I truly kill him, what will all under heaven say of me!
translations.idiomatic: if I truly kill him, what will all under heaven say of me!

sentences.zh: 後世將謂朕何！」

translations.literal: What will posterity say of me!'
translations.idiomatic: What will posterity say of me!"

sentences.zh: 敬宗對曰：「薄昭，漢文帝之舅也，文帝從代來，昭亦有功，所坐止於殺人，文帝遣百官素服哭而殺之，至今天下以文帝為明主。

translations.literal: Jingzong replied: 'Bo Zhao was Emperor Wen of Han's uncle; when Wen came from Dai, Zhao also had merit; his offense was only murder; Wen sent the hundred officials in white mourning to weep while executing him — to this day all under heaven deem Wen an enlightened ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong replied, "Bo Zhao was Emperor Wen of Han's uncle; when Wen came from Dai, Zhao also had merit; his offense was only murder; Wen sent the hundred officials in white mourning to weep while executing him — to this day all under heaven deem Wen an enlightened ruler.

sentences.zh: 今無忌忘兩朝之大恩，謀移社稷，其罪與薄昭不可同年而語也。

translations.literal: Now Wuji has forgotten the great grace of two reigns and plotted to shift the altars of state — his crime cannot be mentioned in the same breath as Bo Zhao's.
translations.idiomatic: Now Wuji has forgotten the great grace of two reigns and plotted to shift the altars of state — his crime cannot be mentioned in the same breath as Bo Zhao's.

sentences.zh: 幸而奸狀自發，逆徒引服，陛下何疑，猶不早決！

translations.literal: Fortunately the treacherous signs erupted of themselves and the rebels confessed — why does Your Majesty still doubt and not decide early!
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately the treacherous signs erupted of themselves and the rebels confessed — why does Your Majesty still doubt and not decide early!

sentences.zh: 古人有言：『當斷不斷，反受其亂。』

translations.literal: The ancients have a saying: 'When you should cut but do not cut, you afterward suffer disorder.'
translations.idiomatic: The ancients have a saying: 'When you should cut but do not cut, you afterward suffer disorder.'

sentences.zh: 安危之機，間不容髮。

translations.literal: The pivot between safety and peril allows not a hair's breadth.
translations.idiomatic: The pivot between safety and peril allows not a hair's breadth.

sentences.zh: 無忌今之奸雄，王莽、司馬懿之流也；

translations.literal: Wuji is today's arch-villain, of the stripe of Wang Mang and Sima Yi;
translations.idiomatic: Wuji is today's arch-villain, of the stripe of Wang Mang and Sima Yi;

sentences.zh: 陛下少更遷延，臣恐變生肘腋，悔無及矣！」

translations.literal: if Your Majesty delays even slightly, I fear revolt will spring at the elbow and armpit, and regret will come too late!'
translations.idiomatic: if Your Majesty delays even slightly, I fear revolt will spring at the elbow and armpit, and regret will come too late!"

sentences.zh: 上以為然，竟不引問無忌。

translations.literal: The emperor thought it reasonable and never summoned Wuji for questioning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought it reasonable and never summoned Wuji for questioning.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，下詔削無忌太尉及封邑，以為揚州都督，於黔州安置，准一品供給。

translations.literal: On day wuchen, an edict stripped Wuji of Grand Mentor rank and his fief, made him protector of Yangzhou, settled at Qian prefecture, with provisions of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: On day wuchen, an edict stripped Wuji of grand mentor rank and his fief, made him protector of Yangzhou, settled him at Qian prefecture, and granted him first-rank provisions.

sentences.zh: 祥，無忌之從父兄子也，前此自工部尚書出為荊州長史，故敬宗以此誣之。

translations.literal: Xiang was a son of Wuji's father's elder brother's line; earlier he had gone out from Minister of Works to Long History of Jingzhou — hence Jingzong used this to frame him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was a son of Wuji's father's elder brother's line; earlier he had gone out from minister of works to long history of Jingzhou — hence Jingzong used this to frame him.

sentences.zh: 敬宗又奏：「無忌謀逆，由褚遂良、柳奭、韓瑗構扇而成；

translations.literal: “Jingzong further memorialized: 'Wuji's treason was fomented by Chu Suiliang, Liu Shi, and Han Yuan stirring it up;
translations.idiomatic: “Jingzong further memorialized that Wuji's treason had been fomented by Chu Suiliang, Liu Shi, and Han Yuan;

sentences.zh: 奭仍潛通宮掖，謀行鴆毒，於志寧亦黨附無忌。」

translations.literal: Shi still secretly communicated with the inner palace and plotted to administer poison; Yu Zhining also clung to Wuji's faction.'"
translations.idiomatic: that Shi still secretly communicated with the inner palace and plotted to administer poison, and that Yu Zhining had also clung to Wuji's faction."

sentences.zh: 於是詔追削遂良官爵，除奭、瑗名，免志寧官。

translations.literal: Thereupon edicts stripped Suiliang retroactively of office and rank, struck Shi and Yuan from the rolls, and dismissed Zhining.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts then stripped Suiliang retroactively of office and rank, struck Shi and Yuan from the rolls, and dismissed Zhining from office.

sentences.zh: 遣使發道次兵援送無忌詣黔州。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent to raise troops along the route to escort Wuji to Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to raise troops along the route to escort Wuji to Qian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 無忌子秘書監駙馬都尉沖等皆除名，流嶺表。

translations.literal: Wuji's son Chong, Director of the Secretariat and imperial son-in-law, and others were all struck from the rolls and exiled beyond the Ling ranges.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji's son Chong, director of the Secretariat and imperial son-in-law, and others were all struck from the rolls and exiled beyond the Ling ranges.

sentences.zh: 遂良子彥甫、彥沖流愛州，於道殺之。

translations.literal: Suiliang's sons Yanfu and Yanchong were exiled to Ai prefecture and killed on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang's sons Yanfu and Yanchong were exiled to Ai prefecture and killed on the road.

sentences.zh: 益州長史高履行累貶洪州都督。

translations.literal: Former Chief Administrator of Yizhou Gao Lixing was repeatedly demoted to Protector of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Former Yizhou chief administrator Gao Lixing was repeatedly demoted to protector of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙申，兵部尚書任雅相、度支尚書盧承慶並參知政事。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day bingchen, Minister of War Ren Yaxiang and Minister of Revenue Lu Chengqing were both made participants in governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on day bingchen, Minister of War Ren Yaxiang and Minister of Revenue Lu Chengqing were both made participants in governance.

sentences.zh: 承慶，思道之孫也。

translations.literal: Chengqing was the grandson of Sidao.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqing was the grandson of Lu Sidao.

sentences.zh: 涼州刺史趙持滿，多力善射，喜任俠，其從母為韓瑗妻，其舅駙馬都尉長孫銓，無忌之族弟也，銓坐無忌，流巂州。

translations.literal: Zhao Chiman, Protector of Liangzhou, was strong of body and skilled in archery, and delighted in chivalrous exploits. His mother's sister was Han Yuan's wife; his uncle by marriage was Chief Commandant of Escort Changsun Quan, a clansman of Wuji's, who was implicated through Wuji and exiled to Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chiman, governor of Liangzhou, was powerfully built and a fine archer, fond of chivalrous adventure. His aunt was Han Yuan's wife, and his uncle by marriage was Chief Commandant of Escort Changsun Quan, a kinsman of Zhangsun Wuji implicated in Wuji's case and banished to Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 許敬宗恐持滿作難，誣雲無忌同反，驛召至京師，下獄，訊掠備至，終無異辭，曰：「身可殺也，辭不可更！」

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong feared that Chiman might stir up trouble and falsely declared that he had rebelled together with Wuji. Chiman was summoned by fast post to the capital, imprisoned, and interrogated with every extremity of torture; he never wavered from his first statement, saying: 'My body may be killed, but my testimony cannot be changed!'
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong, fearing that Chiman might cause trouble, fabricated evidence that he and Wuji had conspired in rebellion. Chiman was summoned posthaste to the capital, thrown into prison, and tortured relentlessly, yet he never changed his story: 'You may kill my body, but you cannot alter my words!'

sentences.zh: 吏無如之何，乃代為獄辭結奏。

translations.literal: The clerks could do nothing about it and so drafted a prison confession on his behalf and submitted it for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks could do nothing further; they forged a confession for the record and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，誅之，屍於城西，親戚莫敢視。

translations.literal: On the day wùxū, he was executed; his corpse was left at the west of the city, and none of his kin dared to look upon it.
translations.idiomatic: On day wùxū he was executed, and his body was left at the city's western gate; not one of his kinsmen dared approach it.

sentences.zh: 友人王方翼歎曰：「欒布哭彭越，義也；

translations.literal: His friend Wang Fangyi sighed and said: 'When Luan Bu wept for Peng Yue, that was righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: His friend Wang Fangyi sighed and said, 'When Luan Bu mourned Peng Yue, he upheld righteousness;

sentences.zh: 文王葬枯骨，仁也。

translations.literal: when King Wen buried dry bones, that was benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: when King Wen buried abandoned bones, he showed benevolence.

sentences.zh: 下不失義，上不失仁，不亦可乎！」

translations.literal: Not to fail in righteousness below, not to fail in benevolence above — is that not acceptable!'"
translations.idiomatic: Surely one may honor righteousness below and benevolence above!"

sentences.zh: 乃收而葬之。

translations.literal: He then recovered the body and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered the body and gave it burial.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，不罪也。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, he did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 方翼，廢後之從祖兄也。

translations.literal: Fangyi was a first cousin once removed of the deposed empress.
translations.idiomatic: Fangyi was a first cousin once removed of the deposed Empress Wang.

sentences.zh: 長孫銓至流所，縣令希旨杖殺之。

translations.literal: When Changsun Quan reached his place of exile, the county magistrate, eager to please his superiors, had him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Changsun Quan reached his place of exile, the county magistrate, eager to curry favor, had him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁卯，詔改《氏族志》為《姓氏錄》。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day dīngmǎo: an edict changed the Records of Clans to the Register of Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on day dīngmǎo, an edict renamed the Records of Clans the Register of Surnames.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗命高士廉等修《氏族志》，升降去取，時稱允當。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Taizong had ordered Gao Shilian and others to compile the Records of Clans, promoting and demoting, including and excluding, in a manner then praised as fair and fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Taizong had commissioned Gao Shilian and others to compile the Records of Clans, ranking and excluding clans in a way then widely praised as fair.

sentences.zh: 至是，許敬宗等以其書不敘武氏本望，奏請改之，乃命禮部郎中禮志約等比類升降，以後族為第一等，其餘悉以仕唐官品高下為準，凡九等。

translations.literal: At this time Xu Jingzong and others, because the work did not record the Wu clan's original standing, memorialized requesting its revision. Li Zhiyue of the Ministry of Rites and others were ordered to rank clans by category, with the empress's clan as the first grade; all others were graded solely by the rank of offices held under Tang, nine grades in all.
translations.idiomatic: Now Xu Jingzong and his allies, noting that the work failed to record the Wu clan's ancestral standing, petitioned for its revision. Li Zhiyue of the Ministry of Rites and others were ordered to re-rank the clans, placing the empress's kin in the first grade and grading all others solely by Tang official rank, in nine tiers.

sentences.zh: 於是士卒以軍功致位五品，豫士流，時人謂之「勳格」。

translations.literal: Thereupon soldiers who through military merit attained fifth rank were admitted to the scholar-official stream; contemporaries called this the 'merit register.'
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers who through military merit attained fifth rank were now admitted to the scholar-official class, a practice contemporaries called the 'merit register.'

sentences.zh: 許敬宗議封禪儀，己巳，奏：「請以高祖、太宗俱配昊天上帝，太穆、文德二皇后俱配皇地祇。」

translations.literal: “Xu Jingzong deliberated on the rites of the Feng and Shan sacrifices. On the day jǐsì he memorialized: 'I request that Gaozu and Taizong both be paired with the August Lord on High, and that the two empresses Taimu and Wende both be paired with the August Sovereign of Earth.'”
translations.idiomatic: “Xu Jingzong drafted the rites for the Feng and Shan sacrifices. On day jǐsì he memorialized that Gaozu and Taizong should both be paired with the August Lord on High, and Empresses Taimu and Wende with the August Sovereign of Earth.”

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，命御史往高州追長孫恩，像州追柳奭，振州追韓瑗，並枷鎖詣京師，仍命州縣簿錄其家。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: censors were dispatched to Gaozhou to pursue Changsun En, to Xiangzhou to pursue Liu Shi, and to Zhenzhou to pursue Han Yuan; all were to be shackled and brought to the capital, and the prefectures and counties were further ordered to register and inventory their households.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, censors were sent to Gaozhou to seize Changsun En, to Xiangzhou for Liu Shi, and to Zhenzhou for Han Yuan; all were to be shackled and escorted to the capital, while local officials were ordered to register and inventory their households.

sentences.zh: 恩，無忌之族弟也。

translations.literal: En was a clansman of Wuji's.
translations.idiomatic: En was a kinsman of Zhangsun Wuji.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，命李勣、許敬宗、辛茂將與任雅相、盧承慶更共覆按無忌事。

translations.literal: On the day rényín, Li Jì, Xu Jingzong, Xin Maojiang, Ren Yaxiang, and Lu Chengqing were ordered jointly to re-investigate the Wuji case.
translations.idiomatic: On day rényín, Li Jì, Xu Jingzong, Xin Maojiang, Ren Yaxiang, and Lu Chengqing were ordered to reinvestigate the Zhangsun Wuji affair together.

sentences.zh: 許敬宗又遣中書舍人袁公瑜等詣黔州，再鞫無忌反狀，至則逼無忌令自縊。

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong further dispatched Palace Draftsmen Yuan Gongyu and others to Qianzhou to interrogate Wuji again on the charge of rebellion; upon arrival they forced Wuji to hang himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong also sent Palace Draftsman Yuan Gongyu and others to Qianzhou to retry Wuji on treason charges; on arrival they drove him to hang himself.

sentences.zh: 詔柳奭、韓瑗所至斬決。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that wherever Liu Shi and Han Yuan were found, they were to be beheaded on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Liu Shi and Han Yuan beheaded wherever they were found.

sentences.zh: 使者殺柳奭於象州。

translations.literal: The envoy killed Liu Shi at Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy executed Liu Shi at Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 韓瑗已死，發驗而還。

translations.literal: Han Yuan was already dead; his corpse was exhumed for verification and the envoy returned.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yuan was already dead; the envoy exhumed the body to verify his identity and returned.

sentences.zh: 籍沒三家，近親皆流嶺南為奴婢。

translations.literal: The property of all three clans was confiscated, and their close kin were all exiled to Lingnan as slaves.
translations.idiomatic: The property of all three families was confiscated, and their close kin were banished to Lingnan as slaves.

sentences.zh: 常州刺史長孫祥坐與無忌通書，處絞。

translations.literal: Changsun Xiang, Protector of Changzhou, was sentenced to strangulation on the charge of corresponding with Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou governor Changsun Xiang was sentenced to strangulation for corresponding with Wuji.

sentences.zh: 長孫恩流檀州。

translations.literal: Changsun En was exiled to Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun En was banished to Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬子，以普州刺史李義府兼吏部尚書、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day rénzǐ: Li Yifu, Protector of Puzhou, was made concurrent Minister of the Civil Service and Grand Counselor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on day rénzǐ, Puzhou governor Li Yifu was made concurrent Minister of the Civil Service and Grand Counselor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 義府既貴，自言本出趙郡，與諸李敘昭穆；

translations.literal: Once Yifu had risen high, he declared that his family originally came from Zhao commandery and arranged seniority with the various Lis;
translations.idiomatic: Once elevated, Li Yifu claimed descent from Zhao commandery and began arranging kinship seniority with various Li clans;

sentences.zh: 無賴之徒藉其權勢，拜伏為兄叔者甚眾。

translations.literal: ruffians who relied on his power and influence bowed and called him elder brother or uncle in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: and countless ruffians who traded on his influence bowed before him as elder brother or uncle.

sentences.zh: 給事中李崇德初與同譜，及義府出為普州，即除之。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Li Chongde had at first been entered in the same genealogy, but once Yifu was sent out to Puzhou, Chongde immediately struck his name from the register.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Li Chongde had initially been entered on the same genealogy, but as soon as Li Yifu was posted to Puzhou, Chongde struck his name from the register.

sentences.zh: 義府聞而銜之，及復為相，使人誣構其罪，下獄，自殺。

translations.literal: Yifu heard of it and bore a grudge; when he returned to office as chief minister, he had men fabricate charges against him. Chongde was imprisoned and took his own life.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yifu heard of this and nursed a grudge; when he returned as chief minister, he had men fabricate charges. Chongde was thrown into prison and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，長孫氏、柳氏緣無忌、奭貶降者十三人。

translations.literal: On the day yǐmǎo, thirteen members of the Changsun and Liu clans connected with Wuji and Shi suffered further demotion.
translations.idiomatic: On day yǐmǎo, thirteen members of the Changsun and Liu clans implicated through Wuji and Liu Shi were further demoted.

sentences.zh: 高履行貶永州刺史。

translations.literal: Gao Lixing was demoted to Protector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lixing was demoted to governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 於志寧貶榮州刺史，于氏貶者九人。

translations.literal: Yu Zhining was demoted to Protector of Rongzhou; nine of the Yu clan were demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhining was demoted to governor of Rongzhou; nine members of the Yu clan were demoted in all.

sentences.zh: 自是政歸中宮矣。

translations.literal: From this time forward, government passed to the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: From this point, power passed to the empress in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔以石、米、史、大安、小安、曹、拔汗那、北拔汗那、悒怛、疏勒、朱駒半等國置州縣府百二十七。

translations.literal: Ninth month: an edict established one hundred twenty-seven prefectures, counties, and protectorates in the states of Shi, Mi, Shi, Da'an, Xiao'an, Cao, Bokhara, North Bokhara, Yidan, Shule, Zhujuban, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, an edict established one hundred twenty-seven prefectures, counties, and protectorates across the Western Regions, including Shi, Mi, Da'an, Xiao'an, Cao, Bokhara, North Bokhara, Yidan, Shule, and Zhujuban.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙午，太子加元服，赦天下。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day bǐngwǔ: the crown prince received the cap of manhood, and an amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on day bǐngwǔ, the crown prince came of age, and the emperor proclaimed an amnesty throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗疾山東士人自矜門地，昏姻多責資財，命修《氏族志》例降一等；

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Taizong resented that gentry of the east prided themselves on pedigree and that marriages often demanded heavy bride-price; he ordered the Records of Clans revised with a rule demoting all by one grade;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Taizong had resented eastern gentry who flaunted their pedigree and marriages that demanded heavy bride-prices; he ordered the Records of Clans revised to demote all clans one grade;

sentences.zh: 王妃、主婿皆取勳臣家，不議山東之族。

translations.literal: princesses' husbands and imperial sons-in-law were all taken from meritorious ministers' families, with no consideration of eastern clans.
translations.idiomatic: princesses and imperial sons-in-law were drawn from meritorious ministers' families, with no regard for eastern pedigrees.

sentences.zh: 而魏徵、房玄齡、李勣家皆盛與為昏，常左右之，由是舊望不減，或一姓之中，更分某房某眷，高下懸隔。

translations.literal: Yet the households of Wei Zheng, Fang Xuanling, and Li Jì all flourished through marriage alliances with them and often supported them; thus old prestige did not decline, and within a single surname branches and affinal lines were further distinguished, with ranks vastly disparate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the houses of Wei Zheng, Fang Xuanling, and Li Jì all prospered through marriage ties with them and often championed their cause, so old prestige never waned; within a single surname, branches and affinal lines were ranked far apart.

sentences.zh: 李義府為其子求昏不獲，恨之，故以先帝之旨，勸上矯其弊。

translations.literal: Li Yifu sought a marriage alliance for his son but failed to obtain one and bore a grudge; he therefore cited the late emperor's intent and urged the emperor to rectify this abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yifu had sought a marriage alliance for his son and been refused; nursing a grudge, he cited the late emperor's policy and urged the throne to correct the abuse.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，詔後魏隴西李寶、太原王瓊、滎陽鄭溫、范陽盧子遷、盧渾、盧輔、清河崔宗伯、崔元孫、前燕博陵崔懿、晉趙郡李楷等子孫，不得自為昏姻。

translations.literal: On the day rénxū, an edict forbade the descendants of Later Wei Longxi Li Bao, Taiyuan Wang Qiong, Xingyang Zheng Wen, Fanyang Lu Ziqian, Lu Hun, Lu Fu, Qinghe Cui Zongbo, Cui Yuansun, Former Yan Boling Cui Yi, Jin Zhao commandery Li Kai, and others to marry among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: On day rénxū, an edict forbade the descendants of such eminent northern clans as the Longxi Li, Taiyuan Wang, Xingyang Zheng, Fanyang Lu, Qinghe Cui, Boling Cui, and Zhao Li from intermarrying among themselves.

sentences.zh: 仍定天下嫁女受財之數，毋得受陪門財。

translations.literal: It further fixed the amounts that might be received nationwide for marrying off daughters, forbidding the acceptance of gate-companion bride-price.
translations.idiomatic: It also capped bride-prices nationwide and forbade the acceptance of gate-companion fees.

sentences.zh: 然族望為時俗所尚，終不能禁，或載女竊送夫家，或女老不嫁，終不與異姓為昏。

translations.literal: Yet clan prestige remained what the age honored, and the prohibition could not finally be enforced: some secretly sent daughters by cart to the groom's house, or kept daughters unmarried into old age, never wedding outside the clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet clan prestige remained fashionable, and the ban could not be enforced: some families secretly sent daughters to grooms' houses by cart, or kept daughters unmarried into old age rather than wed outside the forbidden circle.

sentences.zh: 其衰宗落譜，昭穆所不齒者，往往反自稱禁婚家，益增厚價。

translations.literal: Declining lines dropped from the registers, whom even in seniority and juniority were not acknowledged, often styled themselves forbidden-marriage houses and only raised their bride-prices higher.
translations.idiomatic: Declining branches struck from the registers, whom even their own kin disowned, often styled themselves forbidden-marriage houses and only raised their bride-prices still higher.

sentences.zh: 閏月，戊寅，上發京師，令太子監國。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, day wùyín: the emperor departed the capital and left the crown prince to oversee the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on day wùyín, the emperor left the capital and entrusted the realm to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太子思慕不已，上聞之，遽召赴行在。

translations.literal: The crown prince could not cease his longing; when the emperor heard of it, he hastily summoned him to the imperial train.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince could not cease pining for his father; when the emperor heard of this, he hastily summoned him to join the imperial progress.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，車駕至東都。

translations.literal: On the day wùxū, the imperial carriage arrived at the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: On day wùxū the imperial procession reached the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丙午，以許圉師為散騎常侍、檢校侍中。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day bǐngwǔ: Xu Yushi was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Acting Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on day bǐngwǔ, Xu Yushi was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and acting Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 戊午，侍中兼左庶子辛茂將薨。

translations.literal: On the day wùwǔ, Palace Attendant and concurrent Left Guardian of the Heir Xin Maojiang died.
translations.idiomatic: On day wùwǔ, Palace Attendant and concurrent Left Guardian of the Heir Xin Maojiang died.

sentences.zh: 思結俟斤都曼帥疏勒、朱俱波、謁般陀三國反，擊破于闐。

translations.literal: Sijie irkin Duduman of the Sijie led Shule, Zhujubo, and Yebantuo in rebellion and defeated Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: Duduman, chieftain of the Sijie, led Shule, Zhujubo, and Yebantuo in revolt and defeated Khotan.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以左驍衛大將軍蘇定方為安撫大使以討之。

translations.literal: On the day guǐhài, Left General of the Valiant Cavalry Su Dingfang was made Pacification Commissioner to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: On day guǐhài, Left General of the Valiant Cavalry Su Dingfang was appointed Pacification Commissioner to suppress the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 以盧承慶同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Lu Chengqing was made Grand Counselor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chengqing was made Grand Counselor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 右領軍中郎將薛仁貴等與高麗將溫沙門戰於橫山，破之。

translations.literal: Right Central Commander of the Palace Guards Xue Rengui and others fought the Goguryeo general Wenshamen at Hengshan and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Right Central Commander of the Palace Guards Xue Rengui and others defeated the Goguryeo general Wenshamen at Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 蘇定方軍至業葉水，思結保馬頭川。

translations.literal: Su Dingfang's army reached the Yeyeh River; the Sijie held Matou Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Su Dingfang's army reached the Yeyeh River, where the Sijie held Matou Ford.

sentences.zh: 定方選精兵萬人、騎三千匹馳往襲之，一日一夜行三百里，詰旦，至城下，都曼大驚。

translations.literal: Dingfang selected ten thousand elite troops and three thousand horses and galloped to strike them; in one day and one night they covered three hundred li, and at daybreak reached the foot of the city wall. Duduman was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang chose ten thousand elite troops and three thousand cavalry and raced to strike them, covering three hundred li in a day and a night; at daybreak they reached the city walls, and Duduman was thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 戰於城外，都曼敗，退保其城。

translations.literal: They fought outside the walls; Duduman was defeated and withdrew to hold his city.
translations.idiomatic: They fought outside the walls; Duduman was defeated and retreated to hold his city.

sentences.zh: 及暮，諸軍繼至，遂圍之，都曼懼而出降。

translations.literal: By evening the main forces had arrived in succession, and they surrounded the city; Duduman, in fear, came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: By evening the main army had arrived and surrounded the city; Duduman, terrified, came out and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，定方獻俘於乾陽殿。

translations.literal: Spring, first month: Dingfang presented captives at the Qianyang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Dingfang presented his captives at the Qianyang Hall.

sentences.zh: 法司請誅都曼，定方請曰：「臣許以不死，故都曼出降，願丐其餘生。」

translations.literal: The judicial authorities requested Duduman's execution. Dingfang petitioned, saying: 'I promised him he would not die, and therefore Duduman came out and surrendered; I beg that his remaining life be spared.'
translations.idiomatic: The judicial authorities asked that Duduman be executed. Dingfang petitioned: 'I had promised him his life, which is why he surrendered; I beg that he be spared.'

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕屈法以全卿之信。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'I bend the law to preserve your good faith.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'I will bend the law to honor your pledge.'

sentences.zh: 乃免之。

translations.literal: He then pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He then spared Duduman's life.

sentences.zh: 甲子，上發東都；

translations.literal: On the day jiǎzǐ, the emperor departed the eastern capital;
translations.idiomatic: On day jiǎzǐ the emperor left the eastern capital;

sentences.zh: 二月，辛巳，至并州。

translations.literal: second month, day xīnsì, he arrived at Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: in the second month, on day xīnsì, he reached Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙午，皇后宴親戚故舊鄰里於朝堂，婦人於內殿，班賜有差。

translations.literal: Third month, day bǐngwǔ: the empress feasted kinsmen, old friends, and neighbors in the audience hall, and the women in the inner hall, distributing gifts in graded ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on day bǐngwǔ, the empress feasted kinsmen, old friends, and neighbors in the audience hall and the women in the inner hall, distributing gifts according to rank.

sentences.zh: 詔：「并州婦人年八十以上，綿版授郡君。」

translations.literal: “An edict stated: 'Women of Bingzhou aged eighty and above are to receive silk certificates conferring the title of district lady.'”
translations.idiomatic: “An edict declared that women of Bingzhou aged eighty and above were to receive silk certificates conferring the title of district lady.”
translations.footnote: Closing quotation mark in the source

sentences.zh: 百濟恃高麗之援，數侵新羅；

translations.literal: Baekje relied on Goguryeo's support and repeatedly raided Silla;
translations.idiomatic: Baekje, relying on Goguryeo's backing, repeatedly raided Silla;

sentences.zh: 新羅王春秋上表求救。

translations.literal: the King of Silla, Chunqiu, submitted a memorial requesting rescue.
translations.idiomatic: King Chunqiu of Silla submitted a memorial begging for aid.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以左武衛大將軍蘇定方為神丘道行軍大總管，帥左驍衛將軍劉伯英等水陸十萬以伐百濟。

translations.literal: On the day xīnhai, Left General of the Martial Guards Su Dingfang was made Grand Commander of the Shenqiu Campaign and led one hundred thousand troops by land and sea under Left General of the Valiant Cavalry Liu Boying and others to attack Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: On day xīnhai, Left General of the Martial Guards Su Dingfang was appointed Grand Commander of the Shenqiu Campaign and led one hundred thousand troops by land and sea under Liu Boying and others to invade Baekje.

sentences.zh: 以春秋為嵎夷道行軍總管，將新羅之眾，與之合勢。

translations.literal: Chunqiu was made Campaign Commander of the Yuyi Route and led Silla's forces to join in combined strength.
translations.idiomatic: Chunqiu was made Campaign Commander of the Yuyi Route and led Silla's forces to join the assault.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊寅，上發并州；

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day wùyín: the emperor departed Bingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on day wùyín, the emperor left Bingzhou;

sentences.zh: 癸巳，至東都。

translations.literal: on the day guǐsì, he arrived at the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: on day guǐsì he reached the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 五月，作合璧宮。

translations.literal: Fifth month: the Hebi Palace was built.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, the Hebi Palace was constructed.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，上幸合璧宮。

translations.literal: On the day rénxū, the emperor visited the Hebi Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On day rénxū the emperor visited the Hebi Palace.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以定襄都督阿史德樞賓、左武候將軍延陀梯真、居延州都督李合珠並為冷岍道行軍總管，各將所部兵以討叛奚，仍命尚書右丞崔餘慶充使總護三部兵，奚尋遣使降。

translations.literal: On the day wùchén, Protector of Dingxiang Ashide Shubin, Left Martial Guards General Yantuo Tizhen, and Protector of Juyan Li Hezhu were all made Campaign Commanders of the Lengqian Route, each leading his division to suppress the rebellious Xi; Vice Minister of the Right Cui Yuqing was further appointed commissioner to oversee all three armies. The Xi soon sent envoys to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On day wùchén, Dingxiang protector Ashide Shubin, Left Martial Guards general Yantuo Tizhen, and Juyan protector Li Hezhu were all appointed Campaign Commanders of the Lengqian Route, each leading his troops against the rebellious Xi, while Vice Minister of the Right Cui Yuqing was commissioned to oversee all three armies. The Xi soon sent envoys to surrender.

sentences.zh: 更以樞賓等為沙磚道行軍總管，以討契丹，擒契丹松漠都督阿卜固送東都。

translations.literal: They were reassigned as Campaign Commanders of the Shazhuan Route to attack the Khitan, capturing the Khitan Songmo Protector Abugu and sending him to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: They were reassigned as Campaign Commanders of the Shazhuan Route to attack the Khitan, capturing Khitan Songmo Protector Abugu and sending him to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚午朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Sixth month, first day of the gēngwǔ cycle: there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the first day of the gēngwǔ cycle, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 早午，車駕還洛陽宮。

translations.literal: On the day zǎowǔ, the imperial carriage returned to the Luoyang palace.
translations.idiomatic: On day zǎowǔ the imperial procession returned to the Luoyang palace.

sentences.zh: 房州刺史梁王忠，年浸長，頗不自安，或私衣婦人服以備刺客；

translations.literal: Liang Wang Zhong, Protector of Fangzhou, as the years passed grew increasingly uneasy in mind; at times he privately wore women's dress to guard against assassins;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Liang Zhong, governor of Fangzhou, grew more anxious as the years passed and sometimes wore women's clothing in secret, hoping to evade assassins;

sentences.zh: 又數自佔吉凶。

translations.literal: he also repeatedly divined his own fortune and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: and repeatedly divined his own fortune.

sentences.zh: 或告其事，秋，七月，乙巳，廢忠為庶人，徙黔州，囚於承乾故宅。

translations.literal: When someone reported these matters, autumn, seventh month, day yǐsì: Zhong was deposed to commoner status, exiled to Qianzhou, and imprisoned in Chengqian's former residence.
translations.idiomatic: When word of this reached the court, in autumn, the seventh month, on day yǐsì, Zhong was deposed to commoner status, banished to Qianzhou, and imprisoned in the former residence of Chengqian.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，度支尚書、同中書門下三品盧承慶坐科調失所免官。

translations.literal: On the day dīngmǎo, Minister of Revenue and Grand Counselor Lu Chengqing was dismissed from office on the charge of mishandling tax assessments and allocations.
translations.idiomatic: On day dīngmǎo, Minister of Revenue and Grand Counselor Lu Chengqing was dismissed for mishandling tax assessments and allocations.

sentences.zh: 八月，吐蕃祿東贊遣其子起政將兵擊吐谷渾，以吐谷渾內附故也。

translations.literal: Eighth month: Gar Tongtsen of Tibet dispatched his son Qizheng to lead troops against the Tuyuhun, because the Tuyuhun had submitted to the interior.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Tibet's Gar Tongtsen sent his son Qizheng to lead troops against the Tuyuhun, who had submitted to Tang.

sentences.zh: 蘇定方引軍自成山濟海，百濟據熊津江口以拒之。

translations.literal: Su Dingfang led his army from Chenshan across the sea; Baekje held the mouth of the Ungjin River to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Su Dingfang led his army from Chenshan across the sea, while Baekje held the mouth of the Ungjin River to block him.

sentences.zh: 定方進擊破之，百濟死者數千人，餘皆潰走。

translations.literal: Dingfang pressed the attack and defeated them; several thousand Baekje soldiers were killed, and the rest all broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang pressed the attack and routed them; several thousand Baekje soldiers fell, and the rest fled in disorder.

sentences.zh: 定方水陸齊進，直趣其都城。

translations.literal: Dingfang advanced by land and sea together, striking straight for their capital.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang advanced by land and sea in concert, striking straight for the Baekje capital.

sentences.zh: 未至二十餘里，百濟傾國來戰，大破之，殺萬餘人，追奔，入其郭。

translations.literal: Before they had gone twenty-odd li, Baekje mustered the whole state to give battle; he utterly defeated them, killed more than ten thousand, pursued the fugitives, and entered their outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: Within twenty li of the capital, Baekje mustered its full strength to give battle; Dingfang routed them, killing more than ten thousand, pursued the fugitives, and stormed the outer walls.

sentences.zh: 百濟王義慈及太子隆逃於北境，定方進圍其城；

translations.literal: King Yici of Baekje and the crown prince Long fled to the northern marches; Dingfang pressed forward to besiege the city;
translations.idiomatic: King Yici of Baekje and Crown Prince Long fled to the northern marches while Dingfang pressed the siege;

sentences.zh: 義慈次子泰自立為王，帥眾固守。

translations.literal: Yici's second son Tai declared himself king and led the masses in stubborn defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yici's second son Tai declared himself king and led the defenders in a stubborn stand.

sentences.zh: 隆子文思曰：「王與太子皆在，而叔遽擁兵自王，借使能卻唐兵，我父子必不全矣。」

translations.literal: Long's son Wensi said: 'The king and the crown prince are both still alive, yet my uncle hastily seized troops and made himself king; even if he could repel the Tang army, my father and I would surely not survive intact.'
translations.idiomatic: Long's son Wensi said, 'The king and crown prince are still alive, yet my uncle has seized the army and crowned himself; even if he could drive back the Tang forces, my father and I would not survive.'

sentences.zh: 遂師左右逾城來降，百姓皆從之，泰不能止。

translations.literal: He then led his attendants over the wall to surrender; the common people all followed him, and Tai could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: He led his men over the wall to surrender, and the populace followed; Tai could not hold them back.

sentences.zh: 定方命軍士登城立幟，泰窘迫，開門請命。

translations.literal: Dingfang ordered his soldiers to mount the walls and raise banners; Tai, cornered, opened the gates and begged for mercy.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang ordered his soldiers onto the walls to raise banners; cornered, Tai opened the gates and begged for mercy.

sentences.zh: 於是義慈、隆及諸城主皆降。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yici, Long, and all the city lords surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yici, Long, and all the city lords surrendered.

sentences.zh: 百濟故有五部，分統三十七郡、二百城、七十六萬戶，詔以其地置熊津等五都督府，以其酋長為都督、刺史。

translations.literal: Baekje had formerly had five divisions governing thirty-seven commanderies, two hundred cities, and seven hundred sixty thousand households. An edict established five protectorates including Ungjin on its territory, with its chieftains as protectors and prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Baekje had formerly comprised five divisions ruling thirty-seven commanderies, two hundred cities, and seven hundred sixty thousand households. An edict established five protectorates, including Ungjin, appointing local chieftains as protectors and prefects.

sentences.zh: 壬午，左武衛大將軍鄭仁泰將兵討思結、拔也固、僕骨、同羅四部，三戰皆捷，追奔百餘里，斬其酋長而還。

translations.literal: On the day rénwǔ, Left General of the Martial Guards Zheng Rentai led troops to suppress the four tribes of Sijie, Bayegu, Pugu, and Tongluo; in three battles he was victorious each time, pursued the fugitives more than a hundred li, beheaded their chieftains, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On day rénwǔ, Left General of the Martial Guards Zheng Rentai led troops against the Sijie, Bayegu, Pugu, and Tongluo tribes; victorious in three battles, he pursued the fugitives over a hundred li, beheaded their chieftains, and returned.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，上初苦鳳眩頭重，目不能視，百司奏事，上或使皇后決之。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: the emperor first suffered from dizzying wind, heaviness of the head, and inability to see; when the hundred offices submitted business, at times he had the empress decide it.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, the emperor was first stricken with vertigo, a heavy head, and failing sight; when officials submitted memorials, he sometimes had the empress decide them.

sentences.zh: 後性明敏，涉獵文史，處事皆稱旨。

translations.literal: The empress was by nature keen and perceptive, widely read in literature and history, and in handling affairs always hit the mark of his intent.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was keen-witted, well versed in literature and history, and in every matter she handled met the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 由是始委以政事，權與人主侔矣。

translations.literal: From this time he first entrusted her with state affairs, and her power equaled that of the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he entrusted her with government, and her authority rivaled the emperor's own.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊戌朔，上御則天門樓，受百濟俘，自其王義慈以下皆釋之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, wùxū, the emperor took his seat at the Zetian Gate tower, received the Baekje captives, and from King Yici downward released them all.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the new moon of day wùxū, the emperor mounted the Zetian Gate tower to receive the Baekje captives and released them all, from King Yici downward.

sentences.zh: 蘇定方前後滅三國，皆生擒其主。

translations.literal: Su Dingfang had in succession destroyed three states, each time taking their rulers alive.
translations.idiomatic: Su Dingfang had in succession destroyed three kingdoms, each time capturing their rulers alive.

sentences.zh: 赦天下。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，上幸許州。

translations.literal: On the day jiǎyín, the emperor visited Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On day jiǎyín, the emperor visited Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛未，畋於長社。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day xīnwèi, he hunted at Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on day xīnwèi, he hunted at Changshe.

sentences.zh: 己卯，還東都。

translations.literal: On the day jǐmǎo, he returned to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: On day jǐmǎo, he returned to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以左驍衛大將軍契苾何力為浿江道行軍大總管，左武衛大將軍蘇定方為遼東道行軍大總管，左驍衛將軍劉伯英為平壤道行軍大總管，蒲州刺史程名振為鏤方道總管，將兵分道擊高麗。

translations.literal: On the day rénwǔ, Left General of the Valiant Cavalry Guards Qibi Heli was made Grand Commander of the Peijiang Route Army, Left General of the Martial Guards Su Dingfang was made Grand Commander of the Liaodong Route Army, Left General of the Valiant Cavalry Guards Liu Boying was made Grand Commander of the Pyongyang Route Army, and Prefect of Puzhou Cheng Mingzhen was made Commander of the Roufang Route, leading troops by separate routes to strike Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: On day rénwǔ, Qibi Heli, Left General of the Valiant Cavalry Guards, was appointed Grand Commander of the Peijiang Route; Su Dingfang, Left General of the Martial Guards, Grand Commander of the Liaodong Route; Liu Boying, Left General of the Valiant Cavalry Guards, Grand Commander of the Pyongyang Route; and Cheng Mingzhen, prefect of Puzhou, commander of the Roufang Route — each leading forces by separate routes against Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史劉仁軌坐督海運覆船，以白衣從軍自效。

translations.literal: Liu Rengui, prefect of Qingzhou, was punished for supervising sea transport when ships were lost; he joined the army in plain dress to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengui, prefect of Qingzhou, was demoted after ships were lost under his supervision of sea transport; he entered the army as a common soldier to redeem himself.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙卯，募河南北、淮南六十七州兵，得四萬四千餘人，詣平壤、鏤方行營。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on the day yǐmǎo: troops were levied from sixty-seven prefectures north and south of the Yellow River and in Huainan, obtaining more than forty-four thousand men, who proceeded to the Pyongyang and Roufang field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on day yǐmǎo, troops were levied from sixty-seven prefectures north and south of the Yellow River and in Huainan, raising more than forty-four thousand men who marched to the Pyongyang and Roufang field camps.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以鴻臚卿蕭嗣業為夫餘道行軍總管，帥回紇等諸部兵詣平壤。

translations.literal: On the day wùwǔ, Master of Ceremonies Xiao Siye was made Commander of the Fuyu Route Army and led the troops of the Uyghurs and other tribes to Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: On day wùwǔ, Master of Ceremonies Xiao Siye was appointed commander of the Fuyu Route and led Uyghur and allied tribal forces to Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙未晦，改元。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the last day of the month, yǐwèi, the reign era was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the last day, yǐwèi, the reign era was changed.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙申朔，上與群臣及外夷宴於洛城門，觀屯營新教之舞，謂之《一戎大定樂》。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the first day of the month, bǐngshēn, the emperor feasted with his ministers and foreign tribes at the Luocheng Gate, watching a newly taught dance of the garrison camps, which was called the Music of One Campaign's Great Settlement.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the new moon of day bǐngshēn, the emperor feasted with ministers and foreign envoys at the Luocheng Gate, watching a newly taught garrison dance called the Music of One Campaign's Great Settlement.

sentences.zh: 時上欲親征高麗，以象用武之勢也。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor wished to lead a personal campaign against Goguryeo, thereby symbolizing the momentum of employing arms.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then wished to lead a personal campaign against Goguryeo, symbolizing the momentum of war.

sentences.zh: 初，蘇定方即平百濟，留郎將劉仁願鎮守百濟府城，又以左衛中郎將王文度為熊津都督，撫其餘眾。

translations.literal: Earlier, as soon as Su Dingfang had pacified Baekje, he left General Liu Renyuan to garrison the Baekje prefectural city and appointed Left Guard Central Commander Wang Wendu protector-general of Ungjin to pacify the remaining masses.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Dingfang had just pacified Baekje, he left General Liu Renyuan to garrison the prefectural capital and appointed Wang Wendu, central commander of the Left Guard, protector-general of Ungjin to pacify the remaining population.

sentences.zh: 文度濟海而卒，百濟僧道琛、故將福信聚眾據周留城，迎故王子豐於倭國而立之，引兵圍仁願於府城。

translations.literal: Wendu crossed the sea and died; the Baekje monk Dochan and the former general Boksin gathered masses, seized Zhouliu city, welcomed the former prince Feng from Wa and installed him, and led troops to besiege Renyuan in the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu crossed the sea and died. The Baekje monk Dochan and the former general Boksin rallied forces, seized Zhouliu, brought back the former prince Feng from Japan to crown him king, and besieged Renyuan in the prefectural capital.

sentences.zh: 詔起劉仁軌檢校帶方州刺史，將王文度之眾，便道發新羅兵以救仁願。

translations.literal: An edict recalled Liu Rengui to serve as acting prefect of Daifang and take command of Wendu's forces, sending Silla troops by a convenient route to rescue Renyuan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled Liu Rengui as acting prefect of Daifang to take Wendu's troops and dispatch Silla forces by the nearest route to relieve Renyuan.

sentences.zh: 仁軌喜曰：「天將富貴此翁矣！」

translations.literal: Rengui said in delight: 'Heaven is about to enrich and ennoble this old man!'
translations.idiomatic: Rengui said delightedly, 'Heaven is about to enrich and ennoble this old man!'

sentences.zh: 於州司請《唐歷》及廟諱以行，曰：「吾欲掃平東夷，頒大唐正朔於海表！」

translations.literal: He asked the prefectural office for the Tang calendar and taboo names to take with him, saying: 'I intend to sweep the eastern barbarians level and proclaim the Great Tang's orthodox calendar beyond the seas!'
translations.idiomatic: He asked the prefectural office for the Tang calendar and imperial taboo names to take with him, saying, 'I mean to sweep the eastern lands clean and proclaim the Great Tang calendar across the seas!'

sentences.zh: 仁軌御軍嚴整，轉斗而前，所向皆下。

translations.literal: Rengui commanded the army with stern discipline, fighting in successive engagements as he advanced; wherever he turned, all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui commanded the army with iron discipline, fighting his way forward; wherever he turned, the enemy fell.

sentences.zh: 百濟立兩柵於熊津江口，仁軌與新羅兵合擊，破之，殺溺死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Baekje erected two palisades at the mouth of the Ungjin River; Rengui and the Silla troops struck together, broke them, and killed or drowned more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Baekje erected two palisades at the Ungjin River mouth; Rengui and the Silla forces attacked together, broke them, and killed or drowned more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 道琛等乃釋府城之圍，退保任存城；

translations.literal: Dochan and the others thereupon lifted the siege of the prefectural city and withdrew to hold Imjon city;
translations.idiomatic: Dochan and his allies then lifted the siege of the prefectural capital and withdrew to Imjon;

sentences.zh: 新羅糧盡，引還。

translations.literal: Silla's provisions were exhausted, and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Silla's provisions ran out, and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 道琛自稱領軍將軍，福信自稱霜岑將軍，招集徒眾，其勢益張。

translations.literal: Dochan styled himself General Who Leads the Army; Boksin styled himself General of Frost Ridge; they gathered followers, and their power grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Dochan styled himself General Who Leads the Army and Boksin General of Frost Ridge; as they gathered followers, their power swelled.

sentences.zh: 仁軌眾少，與仁願合軍，休息士卒。

translations.literal: Rengui's forces were few; he joined armies with Renyuan and rested the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui's forces were few; he united with Renyuan and gave the troops rest.

sentences.zh: 上表詔新羅出兵，新羅王春秋奉詔，遣其將金欽將兵救仁軌等，至古泗，福信邀擊，敗之。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting that Silla send troops; King Chunqiu of Silla obeyed the edict and dispatched his general Jin Qin with an army to rescue Rengui and the others; when they reached Gusi, Boksin intercepted and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne to order Silla troops; King Chunqiu of Silla obeyed and sent General Jin Qin to relieve Rengui; at Gusi, Boksin ambushed and routed them.

sentences.zh: 欽自葛嶺道遁還新羅，不敢復出。

translations.literal: Qin fled back to Silla by the Gel Ridge route and did not dare come out again.
translations.idiomatic: Qin fled back to Silla by the Gel Ridge route and dared not venture out again.

sentences.zh: 福信尋殺道琛，專總國兵。

translations.literal: Before long Boksin killed Dochan and alone held command of the state's armies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Boksin killed Dochan and took sole command of Baekje's armies.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁卯，上幸合璧宮。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on the day dīngmǎo, the emperor visited the Hebi Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on day dīngmǎo, the emperor visited the Hebi Palace.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以任雅相為浿江道行軍總管，契苾何力為遼東道行軍總管，蘇定方為平壤道行軍總管，與蕭嗣業及諸胡兵凡三十五軍，水陸分道並進。

translations.literal: On the day gēngchén, Ren Yaxiang was made Commander of the Peijiang Route Army, Qibi Heli Commander of the Liaodong Route Army, and Su Dingfang Commander of the Pyongyang Route Army; together with Xiao Siye and the various barbarian troops they comprised thirty-five armies in all, advancing by land and water on separate routes together.
translations.idiomatic: On day gēngchén, Ren Yaxiang was appointed commander of the Peijiang Route, Qibi Heli of the Liaodong Route, and Su Dingfang of the Pyongyang Route; with Xiao Siye and the frontier armies they mustered thirty-five corps, advancing by land and sea on converging routes.

sentences.zh: 上欲自將大軍繼之；

translations.literal: The emperor wished to lead the great army in person to follow after them;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to lead the main army in person to follow;

sentences.zh: 癸巳，皇后抗表諫親征高麗；

translations.literal: On the day guǐsì, the empress submitted a forthright memorial remonstrating against a personal campaign against Goguryeo;
translations.idiomatic: On day guǐsì, the empress submitted a forthright memorial urging him not to campaign against Goguryeo in person;

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed her advice.
translations.idiomatic: An edict accepted her counsel.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸未，以吐火羅、厭噠、罽賓、波斯等十六國置都督府八，州七十六，縣一百一十，軍府一百二十六，並隸安西都護府。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day guǐwèi, from sixteen states including Tuhuoluo, Yanda, Jibin, and Persia there were established eight protectorates, seventy-six prefectures, one hundred ten counties, and one hundred twenty-six military commissions, all subordinate to the Protectorate-General of the Pacified West.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on day guǐwèi, eight protectorates, seventy-six prefectures, one hundred ten counties, and one hundred twenty-six military commissions were established over sixteen states including Tuhuoluo, Yanda, Jibin, and Persia, all subordinate to the Protectorate-General of the Pacified West.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲戌，蘇定方破高麗於浿江，屢戰皆捷，遂圍平壤城。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on the day jiǎxū, Su Dingfang defeated Goguryeo at the Pei River; battle after battle he was victorious, and he thereupon besieged Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on day jiǎxū, Su Dingfang defeated Goguryeo at the Pei River; victorious in battle after battle, he besieged Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸巳朔，特進新羅王春秋卒；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the first day of the month, guǐsì, the specially advanced King Chunqiu of Silla died;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the new moon of day guǐsì, King Chunqiu of Silla, holder of the specially advanced rank, died;

sentences.zh: 以其子法敏為樂浪郡王、新羅王。

translations.literal: His son Famin was made Prince of Lelang Commandery and King of Silla.
translations.idiomatic: His son Famin was made Prince of Lelang and King of Silla.

sentences.zh: 壬子，徙潞王賢為沛王。

translations.literal: On the day rénzǐ, Prince of Lu Xian was transferred to be Prince of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: On day rénzǐ, Prince Xian of Lu was reassigned as Prince of Pei.

sentences.zh: 賢聞王勃善屬文，召為修撰。

translations.literal: Xian heard that Wang Bo was skilled at literary composition and summoned him as a compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Wang Bo was skilled at composition, Xian summoned him as a literary compiler.

sentences.zh: 勃，通之孫也。

translations.literal: Bo was the grandson of Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Bo was the grandson of Wang Tong.

sentences.zh: 時諸王鬥雞，勃戲為《檄周王雞文》。

translations.literal: At the time the princes were cockfighting; Bo in jest composed a Proclamation Against the Zhou Prince's Cock.
translations.idiomatic: The princes were then cockfighting, and Bo in jest composed a Proclamation Against the Zhou Prince's Cock.

sentences.zh: 上見之，怒曰：「此乃交構之漸。」

translations.literal: When the emperor saw it, he said in anger: 'This is the first step toward sowing discord.'
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor saw it, he said angrily, 'This is the first step toward sowing discord among brothers.'

sentences.zh: 斥勃出沛府。

translations.literal: He expelled Bo from the Pei princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He expelled Bo from the household of the Prince of Pei.

sentences.zh: 高麗蓋蘇文遣其子男生以精兵數萬守鴨綠水，諸軍不得渡。

translations.literal: Goguryeo's Yeon Gaesomun sent his son Namsaeng with tens of thousands of elite troops to guard the Yalu River, and the various armies could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Yeon Gaesomun of Goguryeo sent his son Namsaeng with tens of thousands of elite troops to hold the Yalu, and the Tang armies could not cross.

sentences.zh: 契苾何力至，值冰大合，何力引眾乘冰渡水，鼓噪而進，高麗大潰，追奔數十里，斬首三萬級，餘眾悉降，男生僅以身免。

translations.literal: When Qibi Heli arrived, the ice had frozen solid; Heli led his masses across the water on the ice, advancing with drums and shouts; Goguryeo collapsed in great rout; they pursued the fugitives several tens of li, took thirty thousand heads, and the remainder all surrendered; Namsaeng barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: When Qibi Heli arrived, the river had frozen solid; he led his men across on the ice, advancing with drums and war cries. Goguryeo collapsed; the Tang forces pursued for tens of li, took thirty thousand heads, and the rest surrendered; Namsaeng barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 會有詔班師，乃還。

translations.literal: Just then an edict arrived to withdraw the army, and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then arrived ordering withdrawal, and they returned.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁卯，上畋於陸渾；

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on the day dīngmǎo, the emperor hunted at Luhun;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on day dīngmǎo, the emperor hunted at Luhun;

sentences.zh: 戊申，又畋於非山；

translations.literal: On the day wùshēn, he hunted again at Fei Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: On day wùshēn, he hunted again at Fei Mountain;

sentences.zh: 癸酉，還宮。

translations.literal: On the day guǐyǒu, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On day guǐyǒu, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 回紇酋長婆閏卒，侄比粟毒代領其眾，與同羅、僕固犯邊，詔左武衛大將軍鄭仁泰為鐵勒道行軍大總管，燕然都護劉審禮、左武衛將軍薛仁貴為副，鴻臚卿蕭嗣業為仙萼道行軍總管，右屯衛將軍孫仁師為副，將兵討之。

translations.literal: The Uyghur chieftain Polun died; his nephew Bisudu succeeded to command the masses and, together with Tongluo and Pugu, raided the frontier. An edict appointed Left General of the Martial Guards Zheng Rentai Grand Commander of the Tiele Route Army, with Protector of Yanran Liu Shenli and Left General of the Martial Guards Xue Rengui as deputies; Master of Ceremonies Xiao Siye was made Commander of the Xian'e Route Army, with Right General of the Garrison Guards Sun Renshi as deputy, to lead troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghur chieftain Polun died; his nephew Bisudu took command and, with the Tongluo and Pugu tribes, raided the frontier. Zheng Rentai, Left General of the Martial Guards, was appointed Grand Commander of the Tiele Route, with Liu Shenli, Protector of Yanran, and Xue Rengui as deputies; Xiao Siye was made commander of the Xian'e Route, with Sun Renshi as deputy, to lead troops against them.

sentences.zh: 審禮，德威之子也。

translations.literal: Shenli was the son of Dewei.
translations.idiomatic: Shenli was the son of Liu Dewei.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛亥，立波斯都督卑路斯為波斯王。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on the day xīnhai, the Persian protector Peroz was established as King of Persia.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on day xīnhai, Peroz, protector of Persia, was enthroned as King of Persia.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲子，改百官名：以門下省為東台，中書省為西台，尚書省為中台；

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day jiǎzǐ, the names of the hundred officials were changed: the Department of the Chancellery became the Eastern Terrace, the Secretariat the Western Terrace, and the Department of State Affairs the Central Terrace;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on day jiǎzǐ, official titles were changed: the Chancellery became the Eastern Terrace, the Secretariat the Western Terrace, and the Department of State Affairs the Central Terrace;

sentences.zh: 侍中為左相，中書令為右相，僕射為匡政，左、右丞為肅機，尚書為太常伯，侍郎為少常伯；
