translations.literal: the Attendant-in-Ordinary became Left Chancellor, the Secretariat Director Right Chancellor, the Vice Director Rectifier of Governance, the Left and Right Assistants Respectful Engines, the Director Grand Constant Lord, and the Vice Director Lesser Constant Lord;
translations.idiomatic: the Attendant-in-Ordinary became Left Chancellor, the Secretariat Director Right Chancellor, the Vice Director Rectifier of Governance, the Left and Right Assistants Respectful Engines, the Director Grand Constant Lord, and the Vice Director Lesser Constant Lord;

sentences.zh: 其餘二十四司、御史台、九寺、七監、十六衛，並以義訓更其名，而職任如故。

translations.literal: The remaining twenty-four offices, the Censorate, the nine courts, the seven directorates, and the sixteen guards all had their names changed according to moral glosses, while their duties remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining twenty-four ministries, the Censorate, the nine courts, the seven directorates, and the sixteen guards likewise received new names drawn from moral glosses, though their duties remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，浿江道大總管任雅相薨於軍。

translations.literal: On the day jiǎxū, Grand Commander of the Peijiang Route Ren Yaxiang died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: On day jiǎxū, Ren Yaxiang, Grand Commander of the Peijiang Route, died in camp.

sentences.zh: 雅相為將，未嘗奏親戚故吏從軍，皆移所司補授，謂人曰：「官無大小，皆國家公器，豈可苟便其私！」

translations.literal: As a commander Yaxiang had never memorialized to have relatives or old subordinates join the army; he always referred them to the appropriate offices for regular appointment, saying to others: 'Office, great or small, is all the state's public vessel — how can one casually favor one's private interests!'
translations.idiomatic: As a commander, Yaxiang never sought army posts for relatives or old associates, always referring them to the proper offices for regular appointment. He told others, 'Every office, high or low, is the state's public trust — how can one casually serve private ends!'

sentences.zh: 由是軍中賞罰皆平，人服其公。

translations.literal: From this, rewards and punishments in the army were all even-handed, and men submitted to his fairness.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, rewards and punishments in the army were even-handed, and the troops respected his integrity.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，左驍衛將軍白州刺史沃沮道總管龐孝泰，與高麗戰於蛇水之上，軍敗，與其子十三人皆戰死。

translations.literal: On the day wùyín, Left General of the Valiant Cavalry Guards Pang Xiaotai, prefect of Baizhou and commander of the Woju Route, fought Goguryeo above the She River; the army was defeated, and he and his thirteen sons all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: On day wùyín, Pang Xiaotai, Left General of the Valiant Cavalry Guards, prefect of Baizhou and commander of the Woju Route, fought Goguryeo on the She River; defeated, he and his thirteen sons all fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 蘇定方圍平壤久不下，會大雪，解圍而還。

translations.literal: Su Dingfang besieged Pyongyang for a long time without taking it; when heavy snow fell, he lifted the siege and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Su Dingfang besieged Pyongyang for a long time without success; when heavy snow fell, he lifted the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 三月，鄭仁泰等敗鐵勒於天山。

translations.literal: In the third month, Zheng Rentai and the others defeated the Tiele at Heavenly Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Zheng Rentai and his colleagues defeated the Tiele at Heavenly Mountain.

sentences.zh: 鐵勒九姓聞唐兵將至，合眾十餘萬以拒之，選驍健者數十人挑戰。

translations.literal: The nine surnames of the Tiele, hearing that Tang troops were about to arrive, gathered more than a hundred thousand to resist them and chose several tens of fierce warriors to offer challenge.
translations.idiomatic: The nine Tiele clans, hearing that Tang forces were approaching, mustered more than a hundred thousand men to resist and sent several dozen champions to challenge.

sentences.zh: 薛仁貴發三矢，殺三人，餘皆下馬請降。

translations.literal: Xue Rengui loosed three arrows and killed three men; the rest all dismounted and begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Rengui loosed three arrows and killed three men; the rest dismounted and surrendered at once.

sentences.zh: 仁貴悉坑之，度磧北，擊其餘眾，獲葉護兄弟三人而還。

translations.literal: Rengui buried them all alive, crossed north of the desert, struck the remaining masses, captured three brothers among the yabghu, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui had them all buried alive, crossed north of the desert, struck the remaining tribes, captured three brothers of the yabghu chieftain, and returned.

sentences.zh: 軍中歌之曰：「將軍三箭定天山，壯士長歌入漢關。」

translations.literal: The army sang of him, saying: 'The general's three arrows settled Heavenly Mountain; the stalwart sings his long song as he enters the Han passes.'
translations.idiomatic: The army sang of him: 'The general's three arrows settled Heavenly Mountain; the warrior sings his way home through the Han passes.'
translations.footnote: Closing quotation mark in the source

sentences.zh: 思結、多濫葛等部落先保天山，聞仁泰等將至，皆迎降；

translations.literal: The tribes of Sijie, Dolange, and others had earlier held Heavenly Mountain; when they heard that Rentai and the others were about to arrive, they all came out to welcome and surrender;
translations.idiomatic: The Sijie, Dolange, and other tribes had earlier held Heavenly Mountain; hearing that Rentai was approaching, they all came out to surrender;

sentences.zh: 仁泰等縱兵擊之，掠其家以賞軍士。

translations.literal: Rentai and the others unleashed their troops upon them, plundered their households, and used the spoils to reward the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Rentai and his men then attacked them anyway, plundered their homes, and used the loot to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 虜相帥遠遁，將軍楊志追之，為虜所敗。

translations.literal: The barbarians fled far away in succession; General Yang Zhi pursued them and was defeated by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes fled in succession; General Yang Zhi pursued and was routed.

sentences.zh: 候騎告仁泰：「虜輜重在近，往可取也。」

translations.literal: Scout riders reported to Rentai: 'The barbarians' baggage train is near at hand; go and it can be taken.'
translations.idiomatic: Scouts reported to Rentai, 'The enemy baggage train is near; go and you can seize it.'

sentences.zh: 仁泰將輕騎萬四千，倍道赴之，遂逾大磧，至仙萼河，不見虜，糧盡而還。

translations.literal: Rentai led fourteen thousand light horsemen, pressed forward at double march, crossed the great desert, reached the Xian'e River, saw no barbarians, and returned when provisions were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Rentai led fourteen thousand light horsemen in forced march, crossed the great desert to the Xian'e River, found no enemy, and turned back when provisions ran out.

sentences.zh: 值大雪，士卒饑凍，棄捐甲兵，殺馬食之，馬盡，人自相食，比入塞，餘兵才八百人。

translations.literal: They met heavy snow; the soldiers hungered and froze, cast away armor and weapons, killed horses to eat them, and when the horses were gone men ate one another; by the time they entered the passes, only eight hundred soldiers remained.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow fell; the troops starved and froze, cast away arms and armor, killed their horses for food, and when the horses were gone turned to cannibalism; by the time they reached the frontier passes, only eight hundred men remained.

sentences.zh: 軍還，司憲大夫楊德裔劾奏：「仁泰等誅殺已降，使虜逃散，不撫士卒，不計資糧，遂使骸骨蔽野，棄甲資寇。

translations.literal: “When the army returned, Minister of Justice Yang Deyi impeached them, saying: 'Rentai and the others slaughtered those who had already surrendered, causing the barbarians to scatter and flee; they did not comfort the soldiers or reckon provisions, so that bones covered the wilds and armor was abandoned to supply the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: “When the army returned, Minister of Justice Yang Deyi impeached them, saying that Rentai and his colleagues had slaughtered men who had already surrendered, driving the tribes to scatter; they had neglected the troops and provisions, leaving bones to cover the wilderness and armor abandoned to arm the enemy.

sentences.zh: 自聖朝開創以來，未有如今日之喪敗者。

translations.literal: Since the sacred dynasty's founding, there has never been a defeat and loss like today's.
translations.idiomatic: Since the dynasty's founding, there had never been a defeat as disastrous as this.

sentences.zh: 仁貴於所監臨，貪淫自恣，雖矜所得，不補所喪。

translations.literal: Rengui in what he oversaw was greedy and licentious, indulging himself at will; though he prided himself on what he gained, it did not make up for what was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui, in the territory under his command, had been greedy and licentious; though he boasted of his gains, they did not offset the losses.

sentences.zh: 並請付法司推科。」

translations.literal: He asked that all be handed over to the judicial offices for investigation and sentencing.'"
translations.idiomatic: He asked that all be handed over to the judicial offices for investigation and sentencing."

sentences.zh: 詔以功贖罪，皆釋之。

translations.literal: An edict allowed their merits to redeem their crimes, and all were released.
translations.idiomatic: An edict allowed their merits to redeem their crimes, and all were released.

sentences.zh: 以右驍衛大將軍契苾何力為鐵勒道安撫使，左衛將軍姜恪副之，以安輯其餘眾。

translations.literal: Right General of the Valiant Cavalry Guards Qibi Heli was made Pacification Commissioner of the Tiele Route, with Left Guard General Jiang Ke as his deputy, to settle and gather the remaining masses.
translations.idiomatic: Qibi Heli, Right General of the Valiant Cavalry Guards, was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Tiele Route, with Jiang Ke of the Left Guard as deputy, to pacify the remaining tribes.

sentences.zh: 何力簡精騎五百，馳入九姓中，虜大驚，何力乃謂曰：「國家知汝皆脅從，赦汝之罪，罪在酋長，得之則已。」

translations.literal: Heli selected five hundred elite horsemen and galloped into the midst of the nine surnames; the barbarians were greatly alarmed. Heli then said to them: 'The state knows you were all compelled to follow; your crimes are pardoned — guilt lies with the chieftains; obtain them and that is enough.'
translations.idiomatic: Heli chose five hundred elite horsemen and galloped into the nine clans; the tribes were terrified. He told them, 'The state knows you were all compelled to follow; your crimes are forgiven — guilt lies with the chieftains alone; deliver them and that is enough.'

sentences.zh: 其部落大喜，共執其葉護及設、特勒等二百餘人以授何力，何力數其罪而斬之，九姓遂定。

translations.literal: The tribes were greatly pleased, together seized their yabghu, she, tele, and more than two hundred others and handed them over to Heli; Heli recounted their crimes and beheaded them, and the nine surnames were thereupon settled.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes rejoiced, seized their yabghu, she, tele, and more than two hundred others, and handed them to Heli; he recounted their crimes and executed them, and the nine clans were pacified.

sentences.zh: 甲午，車駕發東都；

translations.literal: On the day jiǎwǔ, the imperial carriage departed from the eastern capital;
translations.idiomatic: On day jiǎwǔ, the imperial procession departed the eastern capital;

sentences.zh: 辛亥，幸蒲州；

translations.literal: On the day xīnhai, he visited Puzhou;
translations.idiomatic: On day xīnhai, he visited Puzhou;

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚申朔，至京師。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on the first day of the month, gēngshēn, he reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the new moon of day gēngshēn, he reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，作蓬萊宮。

translations.literal: On the day xīnsì, the Penglai Palace was built.
translations.idiomatic: On day xīnsì, construction of the Penglai Palace began.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙申，以許圉師為左相。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day bǐngshēn, Xu Yushi was made Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on day bǐngshēn, Xu Yushi was appointed Left Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙丑，初令僧、尼、道士、女官致敬父母。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day yǐchǒu, for the first time monks, nuns, Daoist priests, and female officials were ordered to pay respects to their parents.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on day yǐchǒu, monks, nuns, Daoist priests, and female officials were for the first time required to pay respects to their parents.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊子朔，赦天下。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on the first day of the month, wùzǐ, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the new moon of day wùzǐ, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，熊津都督劉仁願、帶方州刺史劉仁軌大破百濟於熊津之東，拔真峴城。

translations.literal: On the day dīngsì, Protector-General of Ungjin Liu Renyuan and Prefect of Daifang Liu Rengui inflicted a great defeat on Baekje east of Ungjin and captured Jinxian city.
translations.idiomatic: On day dīngsì, Liu Renyuan, protector-general of Ungjin, and Liu Rengui, prefect of Daifang, routed Baekje east of Ungjin and took Jinxian.

sentences.zh: 初，仁願、仁軌等屯熊津城，上與之敕書，以「平壤軍回，一城不可獨固，宜拔就新羅。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Renyuan, Rengui, and the others were encamped at Ungjin city, the emperor sent them an imperial letter, saying: 'The Pyongyang army has returned; one city cannot be held alone — you ought to withdraw to Silla.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Renyuan and Rengui were encamped at Ungjin, the emperor sent an edict: 'The Pyongyang army has withdrawn; one city cannot be held alone — you should withdraw to Silla.

sentences.zh: 若金法敏借卿留鎮，宜且停彼；

translations.literal: If Kim Famin asks that you remain to garrison, you may for the time being stay there;
translations.idiomatic: If Kim Famin asks you to remain and garrison, you may stay for the time being;

sentences.zh: 若其不須，即宜泛海還也。」

translations.literal: if he has no need of you, then you ought at once to return across the sea.'
translations.idiomatic: if he does not need you, then return across the sea at once.'

sentences.zh: 將士鹹欲西歸。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers all wished to return west.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and soldiers all wished to return home.

sentences.zh: 仁軌曰：「人臣徇公家之利，有死無貳，豈得先念其私！

translations.literal: Rengui said: 'A subject pursues the public family's benefit; there is death but no disloyalty — how can one first think of private concerns!
translations.idiomatic: Rengui said, 'A subject serves the state's interest; he faces death but never disloyalty — how can one put private concerns first!

sentences.zh: 主上欲滅高麗，故先誅百濟，留兵守之，制其心腹；

translations.literal: Our lord wishes to destroy Goguryeo; therefore he first executed Baekje and left troops to guard it, controlling its heart and vitals;
translations.idiomatic: Our lord means to destroy Goguryeo; he first destroyed Baekje and left troops to hold it, controlling its heartland;

sentences.zh: 雖餘寇充斥而守備甚嚴，宜□厲兵秣馬，擊其不意，理無不克。

translations.literal: though remaining bandits fill the land and defenses are very strict, one ought to □ sharpen arms and feed horses, strike where they do not expect, and by principle there is nothing that cannot be taken.
translations.idiomatic: though rebels still abound and defenses are tight, we ought to □ drill the troops and feed the horses, strike where they do not expect, and we cannot fail to prevail.

sentences.zh: 既捷之後，士卒心安，然後分兵據險，開張形勢，飛表以聞，更求益兵。

translations.literal: After victory the soldiers' hearts will be at ease; then divide the army to hold strategic points, display our posture broadly, send urgent memorials to inform the throne, and request more troops.
translations.idiomatic: After victory the troops will be steady; then divide forces to hold the passes, extend our position, send urgent dispatches to the throne, and request reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知其有成，必命將出師，聲援才接，凶丑自殲。

translations.literal: When the court knows we have success, it will surely order generals to take the field; as soon as supporting forces arrive, the vicious villains will destroy themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Once the court sees we are succeeding, it will surely send generals; as soon as reinforcements arrive, the enemy will be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 非直不棄成功，實亦永清海表。

translations.literal: This is not merely that we do not abandon achieved success; in truth it will also forever pacify the lands beyond the seas.
translations.idiomatic: We would not merely preserve what we have won; we would truly pacify the eastern seas for good.

sentences.zh: 今平壤之軍既還，熊津又拔，則百濟餘燼，不日更興，高麗逋寇，何時可滅！

translations.literal: Now that the Pyongyang army has already returned and Ungjin is also abandoned, then Baekje's remaining embers will within days flare up again — when can the fugitive bandits of Goguryeo ever be destroyed!
translations.idiomatic: If the Pyongyang army has withdrawn and we abandon Ungjin too, Baekje's embers will flare up again within days — and when will Goguryeo ever be destroyed!

sentences.zh: 且今以一城之地居敵中央，苟或動足，即為擒虜，縱入新羅，亦為羈客，脫不如意，悔不可追。

translations.literal: Moreover, now with the territory of a single city situated in the enemy's center, if we stir so much as a foot we become captives at once; even if we enter Silla we are still detained guests — if things do not go as wished, regret cannot be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, holding one city deep in enemy territory, the moment we stir we become captives; even in Silla we would be mere dependents — and if things go wrong, regret will come too late.

sentences.zh: 況福信凶悖殘虐，君臣猜離，行相屠戮；

translations.literal: Moreover, Fuxin is fierce, perverse, cruel, and tyrannical; ruler and ministers are suspicious and estranged, on the verge of slaughtering one another;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Fuxin is fierce, perverse, and cruel; ruler and ministers are suspicious and estranged and on the verge of slaughtering one another;

sentences.zh: 正宜堅守觀變，乘便取之，不可動也。」

translations.literal: it is exactly the time to hold firm, watch how things change, and seize them when the opportunity comes — we must not move yet.'
translations.idiomatic: this is exactly the time to hold firm, watch how things change, and seize the opportunity when it comes — we must not move yet.'

sentences.zh: 眾從之。

translations.literal: The assembly followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 時百濟王豐與福信等以仁願等孤城無援，遣使謂之曰：「大使等何時西還，當遣相送。」

translations.literal: At that time the king of Baekje, Feng, and Fuxin and the others, seeing that Renyuan and the others were isolated in a city without reinforcements, sent envoys saying to them: 'When will Your Excellencies return west? We shall send you off.'
translations.idiomatic: At that time King Feng of Baekje and Fuxin and the others, seeing that Renyuan and his men were isolated without reinforcements, sent envoys saying, 'When will Your Excellencies return west? We shall send you off.'

sentences.zh: 仁願、仁軌知其無備，忽出擊之，拔其支羅城及尹城、大山、沙井等柵，殺獲甚眾，分兵守之。

translations.literal: Renyuan and Rengui, knowing they were unprepared, suddenly sallied forth and attacked them, capturing their cities of Jiluo and Yin, and the stockades of Dashan, Shajing, and others, killing and capturing a great multitude; they divided their forces to hold these places.
translations.idiomatic: Renyuan and Rengui, knowing the enemy was unprepared, suddenly attacked, capturing Jiluo, Yin, and the stockades of Dashan and Shajing, killing and capturing a great multitude, then dividing their forces to hold these positions.

sentences.zh: 福信等以真峴城險要，加兵守之。

translations.literal: Fuxin and the others, because Jinsian City was strategically vital, reinforced it with additional troops.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxin and the others reinforced the strategically vital city of Jinsian with additional troops.

sentences.zh: 仁軌伺其稍懈，引新羅兵夜傅城下，攀草而上，比明，入據其城，遂通新羅運糧之路。

translations.literal: Rengui waited until they slackened slightly, then led Silla troops by night to the foot of the wall; climbing up by the grass, by dawn they had entered and seized the city, thus opening the route for Silla to transport grain.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui waited until they slackened, then led Silla troops by night to the foot of the wall; climbing up through the grass, by dawn they had seized the city and opened the route for Silla grain convoys.

sentences.zh: 仁願乃奏請益兵，詔發淄、青、萊、海之兵七千人以赴熊津。

translations.literal: Renyuan then memorialized requesting reinforcements; an edict ordered seven thousand troops from Zi, Qing, Lai, and Hai to be dispatched to Xiongjin.
translations.idiomatic: Renyuan then memorialized for reinforcements, and an edict ordered seven thousand troops from Zi, Qing, Lai, and Hai to march to Xiongjin.

sentences.zh: 福信專權，與百濟王豐浸相猜忌。

translations.literal: Fuxin monopolized power, and he and the king of Baekje, Feng, grew increasingly suspicious of each other.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxin monopolized power, and he and King Feng of Baekje grew increasingly suspicious of each other.

sentences.zh: 福信稱疾，臥於窟室，欲俟豐問疾而殺之。

translations.literal: Fuxin claimed illness and lay in a cave chamber, intending to wait until Feng came to inquire after his health and then kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxin claimed illness and lay in a cave chamber, intending to kill Feng when he came to inquire after his health.

sentences.zh: 豐知之，帥親信襲殺福信，遣使詣高麗、倭國乞師以拒唐兵。

translations.literal: Feng learned of this, led his close followers in a surprise attack and killed Fuxin, and sent envoys to Goguryeo and Wa to beg for troops to resist the Tang army.
translations.idiomatic: Feng learned of this, led his close followers in a surprise attack and killed Fuxin, then sent envoys to Goguryeo and Wa to beg for troops to resist the Tang army.
